fileDesc.titleStmt: SAMPLE 1 = THE FLEMINGS IN OXFORD BEING DOCUMENTS SELECTED FROM THE RYDAL PAPERS IN ILLUSTRATION OF THE LIVES AND WAYS OF OXFORD MEN 1650-1690. VOL. II 1680-1690. ED. BY MAGRATH, JOHN RICHARD. OXFORD HISTORICAL SOCIETY 62. 1913.

SAMPLE 2 = THE FLEMINGS IN OXFORD BEING DOCUMENTS SELECTED FROM THE RYDAL PAPERS IN ILLUSTRATION OF THE LIVES AND WAYS OF OXFORD MEN 1650-1700. VOL. III 1691-1700. ED. BY MAGRATH, JOHN RICHARD. OXFORD HISTORICAL SOCIETY 79. 1924.

note.value: 197. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
The want of some considerable News, since the comeing down of Burnyatts has occasion'd my silence ever since. But I can~ot omitt this opportunity by Alderman Simpson, who brought us the good newes of all yor welfares, except Mr Stewardsons, of whom the Town of Kendall, as well as his Relac~ons, may find a loss in time. Sr. I am sensible of the good offices you did my Father of late in agreeing & determining the Controversy betwixt him & Mr Duckett. I wish either of us knew how to make you part of requiteall. The said Mr Duckett & yor Cosen Philipson of Crook clubb'd for a letter to me since ye dissoluc~on of ye Parliamt, wherein they acquainted me that 'twas probable that they might both see us att Oxon~ when the Parliamt mett & hoped wee would make some provision for them. Mr Duckett sayes he has no bussiness, yet heel find some, if weel find him lodgeing. I perceive wee are like to be very throng in Colleges as well as elsewhere, insomuch that the Provost has proffer'd leave of goeing home (or being absent) to as many as please whether of the foundation or not. So I leave it to you whether you are willing yor son should continue with us or not: he shall have conveniency if he stay. 'Tis uncertaine how long the Parliamt will sitt, we hope
theyl be more moderate than the last as to some points. The hurry wee shall be in when they meet, & the fluctuateing condition the Nation is in att prsent (wth some other reasons) may be a meanes to prvaile upon me to decline the Procters place wch comes to our house this ensueing year. I thought I should not have been able to avoid it once, sc: when the Provosts Brother (who is 3 or 4 yeares my Junr, & who was look't upon as ye only competitor) declar'd to me openly & freely 6 weekes ago that he would have nothing to do with it. But since he sayes he has been prvail'd upon to seeke for it, upon prospect of a morall Philosophy Lectures place (worth 500l~ in 5 yeares time) which he may possibly gett, if the Provost continue Vicechancellour another year, it being att the disposeall of ye Vicechancellour & the 2 Procters for the time being, the Dean of Christchurch & the Presidents of Magdalen & St Johns, or any 2 of them & the Vicechancellour. which motive is very considerable & might possibly be a meanes to gett a majority of electors for him in ye College, if I should stand it out. I do designe therefore (partly to avoid all controversy & animosity, & partly to oblige ye Provost by compliance) to desist, & to desire another Publick Lecturers in the Schools,
wch comes to our house att ye Act & is to continue 2 yeares being worth near 30l~ p~ an~u~, which may perhaps prove as advantagious as the other wch is not infallibly certaine: however it will be less prjudiciall to ye body than the Procters place, wch I perceive the Provost is willing his brother should have. Dr Plot is getting Subscriptions for Staffordshire wch is almost ready for the Press, I subscrib'd in ye Holydayes, & any one may subscribe yet, he being in Oxon~ att prsent. The Price will be somwhat higher than that of Oxfordshire. Mr Adams of ye In~er Temple was att Oxon~ lately wth some Proposealls (relateing to ye true meridian Line & measuring all the Countyes in England, wch Project 2 or 3 more are upon) wch I prsume he has sent to you. Besides the Bp of Oxon~s Sermon (preach'd before ye house of Lords) printed att ye Theater, There's a new Book printing at Moses Pitts cost, entitled A Breif Survey of ye late Troubles or Civill Warrs of England (wherein a true account is given of ye Presbyterians) suppos'd to be writt by Sr William Dugdale, but he is not willing to owne it in this juncture. 'Twill be out about Easter & is said to be of 14 or 15s price. If you would dispence with yor concerns in the Country, I could wish you would make a Member in Parliamt, especially seeing 'tis to meet att Oxon~.
Mr Vicechancellour told Mr Simson he should be glad to see you, & so should
Sr Yor most obleiged Freind & Servt
My respects to Mr William & all with you.
I have sent you by ye Bearer the Bps Sermon, Dr Plots proposealls & Sellars proposealls somewhat of ye same nature with Adams's.
This To the Worpfull Daniel Fleming Esq~ att Rydall-hall near Kendall in Westmoreland. Together wth a small Bundle.

note.value: 198. HENRY FLEMING TO DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I receeved by this bearer Mr Simpson 5s who has been very kind to me hear. I doe not question but that you haue heard ere this, what great preparations are made here for the Court. The Vice-Chancelour hath ordered three Colledges for his majesty, the Queen and their attendants scil. Christ-Church, Corpus Christi and Merton. And the rest of the Colledges are or will be soe taken up with other noble men, that it will be very hard for any undergraduats or Batchlours to stay in the University; And if any doe stay in my opinion they had better be away, seing the absent will keep terms (during ye sitting of
ye Parlament) as well as the resident, and alsoe they being soe few in number that I belive they will have noe exercise, nor any opportunity to study, but innumerous temptations to idlenesse and spending mony. Soe all these things considered I desier you yt you would be pleased to lett me come down about Easter, during their sessions. Though I shall be very well contented either to come or to stay according to your pleasure yet I thought fit to acquaint with ye hardships they are like to undergoe which stay. Soe with my duty to your selfe and my love to my brothers and sisters I rest
For Daniel Fleming Esqir at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

note.value: 200. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I recd yor full & ample lettr by ye Bearer Burnyatts (wch made a sufficient compensation for yor late omissions) As also 5£ in money for yor Sons use, which I shall disburse accordingly, and when 'tis gone I know where to gett more without petitioning ye Parliament. I am afraid wee should not speed so well there, if the King can not prvaile upon them to supply his exigencies. Wee hope you are not so low as you would insinuate, seeing you are pleas'd to continue yor ancient noble Token of 5s. wherewith wee shall answer yor expectac~on by drinking his Maties health, the good agreemt of ye King & Parliamt, & yor own personall health & p~sperity. The greatest newes I have not send you att prsent is, That his Maty arriv'd att Oxon~ on Monday last about 5 of ye clock, Only ye Town went to meet him (because 'tis said his Maty did not expect it from ye University) & the Recorder made a Speech to him att his entrance into ye Citty, They prsented him & ye Queen wth each a pair of Gloves. The Vicechancellour & the Docters waited on him ye next morning att Christchurch, & the Publick Orator made a Speech to him in Latin upon his knees, & another in English to ye Queen, wch she seem'd to be very well pleas'd with: After wch they all kisst their Maties hands & prsented them wth rich Bibles. I have subscrib'd for Dr Plots History of Staffordshire upon yor account, & shall take care of it wn it comes out. Sr Wm Dugdales Book (if it be
his) is come out. The price is 13s 6d in sheets, & the Title of it is A view of ye late Troubles, 'Tis an exact narrative of matters of fact, & displays the Presbyterians to the life: wch I suppose is one Reason why Sr William will not owne it in these Times. My Ld of Lincolne has a new Book come out stil'd Brutum Fulmen, wherein he makes Animadversions upon ye 2 Popes Bulls wch excom~unicated Queen Elizabeth & K. Henr: 8. The price is 5 or 6s bound. The Author is expected att or College this week, The Bp of Exeter came last week. I am glad I shall be able to pleasure Sr George Fletchr with my chamber.
I am Sr Yor Faithfull Freind & humble Servt
This To the Worpfull Daniel Fleming Esq~ att Rydall-hall near Kendall in Westmoreland prsent.

note.value: 201. HENRY FLEMING TO DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Yours of Feb. 14 I received with 3l~ and two bookes: and shortly after I received another letter of March 4, by which you acquainted
me of ye death of my Grandmother wch I was very sorry to hear. And by both I understand that you would rather haue me to stay here dureing ye sitting of the Parliamt then to come down into ye country, which I am very willing to doe, if I can haue any studdy to stay in, which I a little fear, if I be put out of this which I haue now, all ye rest being full. On Munday last his Majesty came into Oxon~ with the Queen and tooke up their lodgeings in Xt Church Colledge but this day he goes to Burford too a horse raice, and returns again on Satturday. This with my duty to your selfe and my love to all my brothers and sisters, is all from
For Daniel Fleming Esqir at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

note.value: 204. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Yors dated Aprill ye 6th I recd by ye Post, and am glad to hear of any occasion thats like to draw you into ye South, & that will thereby give us an opportunity of seeing you at Oxon~. I have told the Vicechancellour what great p~bability there is of yor visitting him in May, & he was glad to hear of it. I question whether you may not have begun your journey before these Lines can arrive at Rydall: And therefore in yor absence I have directed them to Mr William, the bussiness of them being only to acquaint you that the Bearer is one Mr Nicholson, Fellow of our College, & one of the main Supporters of Moses Pitts new Atlas. He has newly finish'd one Volume of Germany, whither he had an opportunity to travell not long ago. And he is now going to see his Relac~ons att Plumland in Cumberland, & to see how he likes the Vicarage Bromfeild which ye Bp of Carlisle has p~ferr'd to him, but I suppose heel scarse accept of it. When I was in ye North I desir'd him to look after yor Son Harry, so that I need say no more to recom~end him to you & to desire you to show him the civility of ye Country. I fancy heel but make a short stay in ye North. The Bp of Exeter resign'd up Charleton before he left
Oxon~, which wee have given to ye Provost, instead of Wayhill, wch is undispos'd of yet. I fancy either Mr Crostwhait or Mr Mill will have it. I refer you to ye Bearer for ye rest, & remaine
Fitzharris is like to be try'd this terme, notwithstanding his being impeach'd by ye late house of Com~mons.
This To the Worpfull Daniel Fleming Esq~. att Rydall-Hall near Ambleside in Westmoreland prsent Or in his absence to his Son Mr William Fleming. deliver this.

note.value: 206. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Hopeing yt this letter may finde you at home and in good health after your long journey; According to your order I send you here a note of my disburstments, which I hope will come to your hands before Rich. Burnyeats come from home. As I remember when you were in Oxon~ you told me of a booke you had concerning Philosophy, (but ye name I haue forgott), which I desier you would be
pleased to send me, and also Walkers Partickles, and his Idioms or Phrases, if you can spare them, they being very good bookes, and of a great price. We have had here a very great drought which continues still, all ye ground being soe burnt up, that ye best will scarce quite ye charge of mowing. The first thing in the note (scil. for doeing exercise in ye schools) cost me 20s; 10s of which for ye first day I had of Mr Dixon and Rich. Burnyeats comeing before ye second day, I took 10s out of ye 3l~ wch you sent me by him. And this next week I must doe more exercise, (called Generals) which will cost me allmost 20s, wch I shall pay out of my own mony till Burnyeats come.
Soe with my duty to your selfe, and my love to all my brothers and sisters, I rest
For Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydal-hall near Kendal These
I belive Mr Dixon will send you a note of his disburstments this post.

note.value: 210. HENRY BROUGHAM JUNIOR TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: Great favours do oblige to great acknowledgements, you have been abundant to mee in ye one, and I should show myself most vilely ungratefull, should I be defective to you in ye other: for when I seriously consider ye ineffable kindnesses you have been pleased to bestow on me, who of all have least merited yr favour; I cannot but att ye same time admire ye vastnesse of my debt to you, and wthall repine at mine own inabilities. But since it is not within the limits of my power proportionably to requite yr goodnesse, be pleased (noble Sr) to accept of my humble thanks, which are ye only requitall my small power will permitt me to make. I am infinitely indebted to my Cousin Henry, who has shown great kindnesse and respect to me ever since I came to Oxford. Pray pardon my presumption in giving you this trouble; and call me as I truly am
Your most obliged Cousin and humble Servt
ffor The Right Worshipfull Sr Daniel Fleming living att Rydall nigh Kendall in Westmerland These

note.value: 211. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Your letter I received, and was very glad to hear that you gott well home. I received of Rich. Burnyeats 3l~, and according to your order I sent you an accompt how I disbursed the last by the post, which would haue come to your hands before Burnyeats had begun his journey, if he had not come before his usual time. My cosin Browhams son is come to our College, and intends to stay. We had an election this last term for Tabiters, at which there were two
rejected, and one elected, and there being yet three places void, I belive we shall haue another election the next term. Soe haueing noe news worth trobleing you withall, this with my duty to your self and my love to all my brothers and sisters is all from
Mr Todd is gone into the country who promised to see you.
For Sr Daniel Fleming Knight, at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

note.value: 212. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Since the receipt of yors by ye Bearer (as also of 4£ in money & 5s for a Token, wch wee had in ye Com~on room) I writt to you by Mr Tod, who possibly may not arrive wth you long before this Bearer: However I was unwilling to omit eithr opportunity. I referr'd you in my last to Mr Tod for all late occurrences amongst us. Since he left us our Oxford grand Jury (wch consisted of persons of Quality, as Knights, Esquires & my Ld Norris's brother) found the Bill agt Colledge (ye Protestant Joyner) att the Assizes, though 'twas brought in Ignoramus by such Jury Men as Sheriff Bethel empanell'd. 'Tis
suppos'd that Others (who are clapt up of late for carrying on the same treasonable Designe) may be brought before an Oxford Jury, seeing they have such large Consciences above. Picaring who was clapt up long ago in ye Castle by Dr Lamphire for speaking some dangerous words agt the Govermt, haveing no direct evidence agt him was discharg'd att our Assizes. On Wednesday last I was chosen publick Lecturer for our house for the 2 ensueing yeares, according to what I hinted formerly when I told you of my declineing ye Procters place: & I suppose I shall be Bursar likewise for the ensueing year. Mr Crostwhait has liberty to give up Way-hill att the year end: So that Mr Skeltons Parsonage will be given up before that time, & probably Mr Dentons att Blechington near Oxon~ may fall vacant: which if it do, I suppose Mr Mill will take it, and then I shall have the choice of Mr Skeltons or the liberty to stay till I see what Mr Crostwhait will do about Wayhill which is the much better Liveing, haveing no College
Rent to pay out of it, & but one church, whereas Sherburne (or Mr Skeltons Liveing) has 2 churches upon it, & payes near 40£ p~ an~u~ College Rents. I shall desire my Freinds advice herein, & yours sooner than any ones. I have given my Father some hints as to these particulars. I designe however to do excercise for my Batchler of Divinity's degree the next Terme, & to take it before I accept of prfermt, because it will save compounding. I have spoke to one of ye Composers att ye Theater about altering yor Title in ye 2d Vol: of ye Atlas, & he tells me that the Catalogue is printed att London, & that None but new Subscribers are to be putt in it, because if any of ye old ones should be in, Some might think he impos'd upon ye world in makeing them beleive that there were Two men of ye same Name under different Titles; yet Ile try further if I can prvaile to have it done. However (He sayes) that in ye last Volume all the Subscribers will be printed in it according to their prsent Dignity & Quality. If it can~ot be done in ye Atlas att prsent, I shall endeavour to have it done in Dr Plotts Bookes. My respects to Mr William, & yor Nephew when you see him. I am
Sr Yor much obleiged Freind & humble Servant
To The Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knt att Rydall-hall. near Kendall in Westmoreland. prsent.

note.value: 216. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Yors Dated August ye 19 I recd, in wch if you had not lookt upon an apology as a requisite, att least convenient to be made for yor silence; I should not have expected it, considering ye multiplicity of bussiness you have constantly upon you & othr momentous Reasons
wch I shall not insist on. The bussiness of these lines is to acquaint you that Stephen College (the protestant Joyner) was executed on Wednesday last about 12 of ye Clock according to sentence in a great measure, that is, he was brought out of ye Castle on a Cart to the place of execution wch was between 2 Trees in ye castle-hill-yard, close wthin ye wall, & not by ye high way (as usuall) In wch place (the Rope being about his Neck all ye while) he made a long Speech (I cannot call it a Confession because he did not acknowledge himself guilty of ye Crimes that were laid to his charge & p~v'd agt him) It lasted almost an hour, & was cun~ing worded according to ye opinion of those who gott near enough to hear it. It was (they say) som what of ye Jesuits straine, though he declar'd himself a Protestant of ye Church of England according to its purest reformac~on, that is, from all Superstition & Idolatry, wch wordes he was unable to explaine when he was desir'd to do it by ye Sheriff. He was out of love wth ye Com~on prayer & prtended he found no benefit by it, after it had been read twice or thrice to him in ye time of his respit betwixt Sentence & execution, & though Dr Hall of Pembroke gave him ye Sacramt on Aug. 21. & the Bp visited him once, yet he declar'd a secret love to ye party & complain'd much of being debarr'd ye liberty of haveing Gifted men to cant & pray wth him. Whatever animated his zeal he suffer'd pretty couragiously, & went out of ye world (after he had taken leave of & embraced one Enock a kinsman of his of Trinity College) very quietly wthout ye least hum or acclamac~on. Ketch was very civill to him (thanks to ye 5 Guin~ey's his Relac~ons gave him) permitting him to hang till (in most mens opinion) he was quite dead before
he cutt him down & quarter'd him & burnt his bowells. Most of ye company (wch seem'd to be 2 or 3000) stay'd all ye while. Neither his head nor his Quartrs (wch were carried to London that night) are to be hung up, his Maty haveing remitted ye rigour of ye Law in that particular. The Vicechancellour was close by att his execution & so were a great many othr Doctors & abundance of Masters. Wee know not yet whether the Ignoramus men will be try'd wth us, if they are 'tis suppos'd that Billa Vera may be found agt them though they would not find it agt others. I need not tell you that our freind Dr Oates (now degraded by or newesmongrs to Mr Titus) who was one of Colleges best wittnesses agt the Kings evidence is forbid the Court & remov'd out of Whitehall. 'Tis well if his Tongue, wch he prtends has sav'd ye Nation, do not ruine him upon it, if (as Mudyman sayes) he be a Man that sacrifices all to his passion. I told you in my last that Bletchington was fallen vacant to ye College by the death of Mr Denton, & wee have since given Mr Mill or prsenta~on to it, so that I shall now (as you advise) consider whether I should take
Mr Skeltons Liveing, wch is like to be given up shortly, or wait for Mr Crostwhaits giveing up Way-hill, wch is much bettr & wch he has ye liberty to resigne att Midsum~r if he please, or run ye risk of looseing both & being Senior ffellow. I am
Sr Yor most obleiged Freind & Servt
To The Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Ridall-Hall in Westmoreland prsent.

note.value: 218. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: Since the receipt of yors by Burnyatts I have not had much Newes to send you, which has occasion'd my silence thus long. I confess I had an opportunity of writeing to you by Mr Fishers brother, but, it happend, that I was very bussy then, which made me omitt it. But I can~ot wave this, seeing Mr Nicholson the Bearer (who is going to take possession of Mr Sills prebendary, &, if he please, of Turpenhow also) comes close by yor door. I need not give you any character of him, or send any newes by him, because hees able to furnish you with all occurrences that have happen'd among us of late. Heel acquaint you with the reasons why I passt by Mr Skeltons Liveing of late. As also why he may perhaps refuse Turpenhow. Dr Lamphire, our History professor is much troubled wth a delirium, so that 'tis thought his place may be in the disposeall of ye Convocation e're long. I reserve the rest till the returne of Burnyatts, who setts out about Thursday or fryday next. and remaine
These To the Right Honorable Sr Daniel Fleming Knt att Rydall-hall in Westmoreland prsent.

note.value: 219. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Since yors by the Bearer (by whom I receiv'd 7l~ for the use of yor Son & the old Quantum for an health wch wee spent on ye 5th of Nov:) I writt to you by Mr Nicholson who is come to take possession of Mr Sills prebendary & Turpenhow too wee fear, if you do not disswade him from it, wth the considerac~on of greater things in ye South in due time. I acquainted you by him that I had forgone Sherburne (Mr Skeltons Liveing) in hopes either of Way-hill at Midsum~er, if Mr Crostwhait give it up then, or of being Senior ffellow, if he do not. The event must show whether I have done well or ill in it. I would act for the best as farr as I am able to judge, & my Freinds are pleas'd to advise. I am very well satisfy'd wth my condition att prsent, & would not change it, unless I thought I could mend it, wch possibly may be difficult to do. I remember what the Justice of Stainbankgreen writt to me sometime after he was possesst of the estate & a good wife, sc: you are well if you know when you are well , which words (comeing from a plain down-right honest Man) may perhaps have more in them than wee are aware. However theyl require considerac~on, & accordingly I have done it in wavering the above menc~on'd Vicarage. I think I told you in my last that Dr Lamphire Principall of Hart-hall was much indispos'd & crazy in his head, & his distemper continues upon him still, so that severall are menc~on'd both for the History professors place (wch is worth an 120 or 140l~ p~ an~u~ besides a considerable fine) & the Hall. The latter is in ye disposeall of the Chancellour & the former of ye Convocation. Wee are like to have an election this Terme both for ffellows & Tabiters. I can~ot foresee how things will go yet, yor Son has 4 Seniors (if the Chancellours Son
of Carlisle who is clark of ye College stand) & I know not what number wee shall pitch upon yet, I wish you would hasten Mr Nicholson up: he might help att a dead lift. I am
Sr Yor faithfull Freind & humble Servt
These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knt: att Ridall-hall in Westmoreland prsent

note.value: 220. HENRY BROUGHAM JUNIOR TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
When I seriously consider yr unspeakable kindnesse to me and compare yr goodnesse with my unworthinesse, I cannot but infinitely admire my ingagements to you, and with all repine at mine own inability of making requitall: therefore give my pen leave (Most Noble Sr) to return you what I can, my heartiest thanks for all ye
fresh tokens of yr love, in particular for ye last; besides ye obligac~on of which, you were pleased to confer the happinesse and honour upon me of reading yr lines; wch I did never so much as expect to aspire to, knowing how much it was below ye greatnesse of yr person to take such a trouble upon you, and how little I have meritted such a favour at yr hands. My humble duty to you, craving yr pardon for this scrible, and desireing you to doe me the right as to think me
ffor The right Worshipfull Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydall nigh Kendall in Westmrland These

note.value: 221. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Yours of Octob. 6. 81 with 3l~ and two bookes and Cloth for Suit and studying gown I received which will doe very well. I belive we shall have an election for tabiters betwixt this and Christmas, but how things will be carried at it I doe not know. We haue been latly afraide of looseing Mr. Dixon, for ye last week Mr Skelton resigned up his parsonage which Mr Dixon had some thoughts of takeing, but haueing refused it Mr Simpson his im~ediate junr hath taken it. On Munday last Mr Nicholson went towards Carlile, the Bishop their haueing sent for him to make him prebend, and to giue him a parsonage called Terpenne in Cumberland. Soe haueing noe news
worth writeing, with my duty to your self and my love to all my brothers and sisters I rest
For The right worshipfull Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

note.value: 222. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Haveing had an Election yesterday both for Fellows & Tabiters, I think my self obleig'd to let you understand how things went, though the latter did not descend so low as yor Son: I spoke to Mr Provost in behalf of him, but he said he was afraid (considering what Seniors we had, & how many Tabiters wee had already, & how many Fellows were like to be taken in) wee could not stretch for him att prsent, but he has p~miss'd to do him a kindness assoon as possible; sc: when the first Tabiter goes of, which will be att Act next p~bably, or att Michaelmas att furthest. Wee elected 2 Tabiters, sc. Jackson & Hartly & left one Highmore (who is 2 or 3 terms yor Sons Senior) unelected before him. So that if he continue to appear att the next election wee shall make up 9 Tabiters rather than yor Son shall stay behind or lose any time. I am sure the provost will do it. ffour Masters sc. Mr Scot, Mr Clark
(who I wish may deserve it) Mr Addison & Mr Smith were elected Fellows, & are to be admitted on St Tho: day. Mr. Nicholson is not return'd as yet out of yor parts. If he take Turpenhow, he is not like to have the same liberty with Mr Crostwhait of giveing it up at ye year end. I recd a lettr lately (wch I show'd ye Provost) from Rich: Duckett, wherein he acquaints us that there's 193l~ decreed agt Anthony Saul & Robt Gibson of Heversham for our college, & that since the Decree there's 6l~. 13s. 4d for 7 or 8 yeares accrueing in Mr Wilsons hand. Mr Provost said he had writt to you about some such thing.
I know not what to make of it though I am Bursar. Dr Lamphire of Hart-hall is somwhat recoverd of his distemper. I am
These To the Right Honourable Sr Daniel Fleming Knt att Rydall-hall near Kendall in Westmorland prsent.

note.value: 224. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I hope 'tis not too late to wish you an happy New-year, & to acquaint you that yors bearing date Dec: 9 & 10th came to my hands on Dec: 24th. I have been the longer in returning an Answer, because Mr Vicechancellour was out of Town in ye Holydayes, & I was willing to let him know (before I writt) how carefull you had been in manageing ye College concerns in relac~on to Heversham exhibitions, and he is infinitely pleas'd with what you have done therein, & is thankfull to you for yor good endeavours to serve ye College upon all occasions. I fancy yor Cosen Nicholson will have much ado to p~cure yor pardon for his not calling upon in his returne to Oxon~, seeing he came through Rydall, He misst my Fathers house likewise, & posted on (att ye rate of an Oxford Hackney) to Kendall that night in hopes to meet a fellow-traveller, who fail'd him when all was done, & wee think he was right serv'd. It seemes he took Instituc~on into Turpenhow as well as ye Prebendary before he left ye North, So that you are like to have him among you again e're long. I perceive wee shall not be able to hinder him from entering upon his year of Grace very shortly: One would think there were a neice in ye case, he is so hasty. Hees gone to Exeter att prsent wth
the Bps Son, whom Mr Provost sent home for fear of ye worst, he haveing expresst some good likeing to a young Gentlewoman (wth in 12 miles of Oxon~) wth whom he happen'd to converse in ye Christmas Holydayes. I suppose the young man will scarce returne this half year, if at all, But Mr Nicholson will be back wthin a fortnight: Mr Mill, who took his Drs degree since he had Bletchington, is att London. Dr Plotts Staffordshire is not like to be publish'd these 2 months yet as farr as I can perceive: when it comes out weel endeavour to fulfill yor orders. 'Tis well if the second Volume of Germany come out before the Author setle amongst you. Mr Tully of or house who is upon his year of Grace, & who was lately wth the ArchBp of York, has left his Grace, intending to live with an Oxford Gentlewoman (whose name was Witt) haveing been married to her
above a Quarter of a year ago. He has gott 3 prebendary's (2 in York, & 1 att Rippon) of ye Arch Bp, dureing his short abode wth him: but he wants a parsonage yet. I need not tell you that my Ld Preston is to go to Ambassadour into France, or that his brothr Mr Graham of Ch: Church is preferr'd by him lately to a parsonage in yor Country, or upon the edge of Cumberland) vacant by ye death of Mr Usher Senr. My respects to Mr William. I am
Sr Yor much obleiged Freind & Servant
Pray prsent my duty to my Father when you see him & my respects to Justice Fisher, acquainting them, if you please, that I shall write to them both shortly.
These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knt att Rydall-hall near Kendall in Westmoreland

note.value: 225. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Yours of Jan. ye 25 I received, and according to your order I acquainted Mr Todd with that you mentioned in your letter, and he
promised to satisfie you in it as well and as shortly as he can. We haue here no news as yet of a Parlament but it is supposed that when there is one, it will be at Oxford. I haue enclosed a note of my disburstments, wherein perhaps you may think some things dear, yet I am certain yt I haue had every thing now as cheap, and many cheaper, then formerly I haue had, when left upon the score. Soe haueing noe news to acquainte you with, but that all your friends here are well, with my duty to your selfe, and my love to all my brothers and Sisters I rest
For The Right Worshipfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydal-hall near Kendal These

note.value: 227. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Yors dated Feb: the 18th I recd, by Sr Fisher, who arriv'd safely wth us, & is now fallen to his old trade of Rendring, which will hold him tugg for one 2 or 3 yeares. The slavery is not so great, but that there will be alwayes some found who will be willing to undergo it, so long as it qualifies men for prebends & good Liveings. Your Cosin Nicholson has time to consider of Turpenhow till Lady Day, att which time he must declare whether heel stick by it, or his ffellowship. The Bp makes new offerrs and p~misses to him which I fancy will obleige him to quit his great priviledges belonging to a ffellow, & enter upon his year of Grace att Lady Day, wch may prove somwhat ominous. He is like to have Father Graham for his neighbour, his Brother (the Ld Preston) haveing bestow'd upon him a good parsonage (wch Mr Usher had) upon ye Borders, which he has either taken possession of already, or is comeing down to do it. Mr Ward, who was out of his ffellowship att St Tho: day last, is lately married to one Ayleworth's
daughter (a chandler in Oxon~) with whom I am afraid he has gott no great matter. 'Tis generally observd that our Oxford matches are but indifferent, & his Liveing being so too, heel have grow rich in hast. I can~ot learne as yet when Dr Plots Staffordshire is like to come abroad. Dr Busby's old proposalls about a Catechetick Lecture are on foot again, & 'tis suppos'd theyl take in Congregation & Convocation: the Stipend is 80l~ p~ an~u~ for 20 Lectures. His Maty is like to be att Newmarkett & Windsor till October. 'Tis said his Royall Hness is to meet ye King att Newmarkett. I am
These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knt: att Rydall-hall near Kendall in Westmoreland. prsent.

note.value: 229. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
In answer to yors by Sr Fisher I writt by Mr Simpson of Kendall on March ye 6th: Since which time I receiv'd one from you by ye Bearer (His Excellency the Northerne Ambassadour, who makes as much noise in our parts, as his Brother the Emperour of Fez & Morocco dos elsewhere) as also five pounds in money for the use of yor Son & 5s as a Token, wherewith as many of ye company as were att home drunk yor health one fryday night, when I treated them with cold Capon & chine that were sent to me as presents being Bursar.
My brother Bursar, our proctor, has gott the Morall philosophy Lecturers place, which as I told you formerly will be worth an 200l~ p~ an~u~ to him for five yeares, if he continue so long in ye University, & have no cura Animaru~ upon him. His being Senior Proctor & his brother the Vice-chancellour secur'd it to him. I am to read as often as he for 25l~ p~ an~u~ for 2 yeares. If Way-hill be given up att Midsum~er & I accept of it, mine will hold as long as my year of Grace. Mr Nicholson has time given by ye College of considering till Whitsuntide what heel do about Turpenhow, & if he stick to it then, his year of Grace is to com~ence from Lady day last past. Dr Busbys Catechetick Lecture is referr'd to Delegates of Convocation (in number 27) who are to adjust matters & difficulties about it & to report them to ye Convocation in order to their approveing or not approveing of the Amendments, 'tis thought theyl hardly qualify it so as to make it pass. Yor Son had some fitts of ye Ague a little while ago, but they are over God be thank't. The money you sent for his use will overdo at present: you shall know how things stand wth us before the next returne of ye Bearer. I am
Sr Yor much obleiged Freind & humble Servant
These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knt att Rydall-hall in Westmoreland. prsent.

note.value: 232. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Haueing soe fit an opportunity I could not willingly lett it pass without troubleing you with a line. I haue had the ague againe since
the last time I write to you, but it did not trouble me long till I gott it cured. I suppose we shall haue an election for Tabiters the next terme, but how many will be elected (whether one or two) t'is not yett known, if two I shall then know my fate, haueing but one Senior and being myself sanding already for Batchlour of Arts. These cloths which I haue being almost worn, I mut desier you that you would be pleased to send me cloth for a suite the first opportunity. Soe with my duty to your self and my love to all my brothers and sisters I rest
For The Right worshipfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

note.value: 233. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Haveing not writt to you since the returne of Burnyatts, I am afraid youl think me negligent. If I had had time I would have writt to you by Mr Nicholson of our house, who, upon ye Bps request came down into ye North about a month ago, & is since return'd. He was at ye Synod & Visitac~on in Carlisle, but came no nearer you than Kendall, where he forgott to leave a lettr for my fathr either in his going downe or comeing up. I fancy heel give up ye Vicarage (& consequently the Neice) when all's done, & stick only to ye Prebend (wth ye Bps good leave) & his ffellowship, wherewith I perceive the Chancellours place is likewise consistent, if he can catch it. The College will expect to know what heel do att Whitsuntide, as also what Mr Crostwhait will do att Midsum~er. Dr Plotts Staffordshire is not like to come out for some time yet. Dr Busby's Catechetick
Lecture dos not come to any thing as yet, though it has been twice canva'sst in Convocation, severall of the Authors proposealls were rejected & new ones agreed to in their place; yet there are severall heads undetermin'd, wch the young Mastrs & the Grave Don~s could not agree vpon, & 'tis question'd whether theyl come to any resoluc~on in the point. Yor Son has had some fitts of ye Ague since Burnyatts left us, but he is quite rid of them now, God be thankt. I am
These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydall-hall near Kendall in Westmoreland. prsent.

note.value: 234. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I writt to you about 10 dayes ago by Mr Simson of Kendall, and the Morrocco Ambassadour haveing been with us lately, I think myself obleig'd to give you some account thereof. He came from Windsor on the 30th of May, and (being invited) calld in at Sr Timothy Tyrrills att Shotover where he stay'd about an hour,
& where Dr Hide of our house & publick Library Keeper, (who sent him our Liturgy in Arabick to London & has held correspondence wth him in his own Language by lettrs) met him in a coach & satt next to him on one hand att ye Table: Att his comeing out of Sr Timothys grounds, he was mett by above an 100 horse out of Oxon~ on Shotover hill, all which were led up in order & marshall'd by one Capt Woods, (an experienc'd Souldier in ye late Warrs & now Butler of Christ Church) next to whom Dr Yerbury of Magdalens (who made a short Speech in English to his Excellency) came up, & the rest in order (being most of them Gentlemen Com~oners, Noblemen & Mastrs of Arts). They brought him into ye Citty a little before 8 of ye clock att night, he was attended likewise by 4 or 5 coaches. The Streets & Windows were as much crowded as when his Maty came to Town, if not more, They hum~'d him as he came up the Street, & afterwards when he lookd out of ye Dineing Room in ye Angell from whence he seem'd to behold the Schollers & great numbers of people in the streets with great satisfaction, laughing att them heartily. Shortly after his arriveall att ye Angell the Vicechancellour & Drs waited on him, & Mr Wyatt (the Univrsity orator) made a short speech to him in Latin, the substance of which being interpreted to him he prsently made a reply to this effect, That upon his Maty's invitac~on he was come to see the Univrsity, & that he was sensible how loyall they were or else he would not have visited them, & that he thank them for their civilities & would acquaint his Maty therewith. The next
morning he sent word to the Vicechancellour that he would give him a visit, wch he accordingly did about 8 of ye clock: Wee had ye great Gates open for him & made a lane betwixt them & the chappell wch he passd through, & view'd first the chappell, then Sr Josephs Buildings, and then the Hall, where the Horne was prsented to him full of Ale, wherein they drunk his health, but he refus'd to drink himself, jesting in his own country language & proverb, God deliver him from Horns . From our College he went down to the Physick Garden, & view'd Magdalen College, then New College, then Wadham, then St Johns and Trinity and some other Colleges all before Din~er. After din~er about 4 of ye clock (the Convocation Bell haveing done att three) he came to the Theater, which, in my opinion, was fuller of Schollers, Strangers & Ladies than att Act, where he was entertain'd first with Wind Musick in ye Staires (as the Prince of Orange was before him long ago) then with a long Speech in Latin by ye Orator, after which the Proctor read his Matys Letter to ye Convocation, wherein he desir'd the Univrsity to show him all the respect imaginable. Then a Coppy of Verses (in ye Com~endac~on of Africa) were spoken by one Mordant Student of Ch: Church & brothr to the Ld Mordaunt: after
wch he was entertain'd with Musick both Vocall & Instrumentall, & then that Solemnity ended: He was plac'd in ye Vicechancellrs Seat or rather equall to it, His Interpreter (who is an English Renegado & had his pardon granted him before he durst come over) standing by him. There were severall of his Retinue in their uncouth Garbs & Turbants not farr from him. From ye Theater he went to ye Convocation house & Divinity School & so to the Library, where Dr Hide aforemenc~ond made a Speech to him in Arabick (or in his own Language) wth wch he was hugely pleas'd, as also wth the Arabick Books wch he show'd him afterwards. From the Library he went to see severall Colleges & particularly Christ Church, where the Bp gave him a collation. He went out this morning about 7 of ye clock, and is to dine (as 'tis said) wth my Ld Norris at Rycaut. The Univrsity gave him no Treat (because his Maty was agt it) but they prsented him with 5 Arabick Books & the Cutts of ye Colleges all richly bound, the names of 3 of ye Bookes were Avicen's philosophy, Euclids Elements & the Nubian Geography:
They cost 20s a peice binding. He seem'd so well pleas'd wth them and wth the Civilities shown him, that he p~missd Dr Hide that, if there were any Books in all Africa wch the Univrsity wanted & had a mind to have, he would do his utmost to procure them for them. So the Dr has given him the names of some Books, wch 'tis thought heel send: He being a man of great integrity & very religious, haveing prayrs 5 times a day and night together. He has a Melancholy thoughtfull look, & is not so Tawny as the rest by much, he wears a thin kind of Turbant on his head, & a kind of Slippers on his feet, being bare legg'd, & haveing rich Lin~en or a loose Garmt rowl'd about his Body; he has a stately gate (though he was in his Coach all but in ye Colleges) & seemes to be somwhat above 30 yeares of age. He eats no flesh but very much parch't & of his own Cooks dressing, his usuall Liquour is milk & water, So that if he knew of his Interpreters being drunk with wine (on ye 30th, as they say he was & fell of his horse) it would go near to cost him head. He expresses a huge esteem & veneration for his Maty upon all occasions, & they say the King & the Duke have a very great respect for him. I am afraid I have been too tedious & therefore crave leave to remaine
These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knt att Rydall-hall near Kendall in Westmoreland

note.value: 235. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
In my last on June ye 1st. I gave you an account of the entertainmt of the Morrocco Ambassadour att Oxon~, which, I prsume, you have since receiv'd in print in ye Gazett. The bussiness of these Lines is to give you an account of Way-hill, wch Mr Crostwhait has thought fit to part with & resigne to the great admirac~on both of ye College & the University & some say of the Bp of Oxon~ likewise, who it seemes was heard to say att the Visitac~on att Bister this week, that if one of his house should have done so, he would have turn'd him out im~ediately. The Provost, upon his giveing of it up, desir'd me to carry him to ye Taverne & give him as much wine as he could drink, that he might say he was not himself when he did it: Severall other Remarks have been made upon it both by him & others. So that I am in a man~er necessitaten to take it to avoid such imputac~ons & reflections. I confess I could have been as well content, if he had kept it, but seeing he did not, it would seem neither wisdom (nor perhaps policy) in me to forego it: And upon these considerac~ons, as also upon the advice of very good freinds, I made my application to the company for it, & they have unanimously given it to me (as also a year of Grace ending att the last of July come a twelve month) & I have accordingly treated for it: & shall be obleig'd, I am afraid, (to prevent damages & inconveniencies that may arise from Sequestrac~ons & the neglect of letting it, the harvest being att hand) to take Instituc~on & Induction sooner than I design'd. Ile gett an election for Tabiters if I can before I lose my vote. However Ile do my utmost in hastening of it upon yor Sons account, who I know is as sure of it as if he had
it. I have spoken to the Provost already & he has p~miss'd to be mindfull of him & I know the fellows, att least a majority of them (but I fancy all) will be ready to befreind him. So that I do not doubt but he is as sure of it as I am of Way-hill, The profittes whereof come in partly by Glebe & Tythes, & partly by a Fair, which in 2 dayes (every Michaelmas) brings in 50 or 60l~. All which the Provost lett for 215l~ that year he had it. I question whether it may be sett for so much again, yet I fancy it will prove as good as a double ffellowship. The worst thing belonging to it is a bad house, which I may possibly rebuild in time as my Revenues come in, & so make some returns of gratitude to the College. I have not time to send you the particulars of yor Sons accounts att prsent, because I am employ'd about my Latin Sermon, which I am to preach for my Batchler of Divinity's degree: which I designe to take before Instituc~on & Induction to prevent charges of compounding in the University where I think of staying till my year of Grace be out, & where I could have liv'd contentedly if my senior had thought fit to march of, & had not thrown such a great temptac~on in my way. It would look like too great a peice of self-denyall to forgo it, & I hope by accepting of it both to answer the designe of the Founder, & to discharge a good Conscience, which will be more satisfactory than any thing perhaps I could oppose to my self in renounceing of it. Wee must not all
expect to be Vice-chancellours, & 'tis hazardous waiting for dead mens shooes. I am
These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydall-hall in Westmoreland.

note.value: 239. HENRY BROUGHAM JUNIOR TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: I would make an apology for this my second presumption, but that I think I should be much awanting to my self, if I did not sometimes kiss your hand with a letter, not only to discharge my duty, but also to make my gratefull and humble acknowledgemts for the many, fresh and signall tokens of your love. But if for all this, this paper be resented as a trouble by you, I must beg pardon of that same goodness, wch induced me hereunto, when I considered that you were pleased to descend so low, as by yr last kindness to remember me the most unworthy of all those that rest obliged to you. Pray tender my humble service to all my Cousins; and though I could never aspire to that honour and happinesse as to be acquainted with any one of them; yet give me leave to tell them, they have an unknown friend, whose life and fortunes are totally devoted to all their services. After my humble duty to you, give me leave to subscribe my self,
Yr most obedient Godson & Obliged Servant
For The right worshipfull Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal in Westmorland. These

note.value: 240. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Since yors by the Bearer (by whom I recd 4l~ in money for yor Sons use & 5s for a Token which those shall pertake of who can befreind yor Son) I writt to you by my brother James: & receiv'd one from you by the post on July ye 12th, wch bore date July ye 1st :
in which I am sensible how reall a well-wisher you are to me, & have ever since been the better pleas'd with my choice of Way-hill, because you approve of it. I have not been able to prvail for an election of Tabiters this Terme. The Provost being full of bussiness, & being likewise willing to observe the old Rule of haveing as many elections att the same time as may be. So that I do not doubt but the next Terme will p~duce some Tabiters as well as a ffellow & a chaplain: yor Son must have patience in the mean time, & weell make what p~gress wee can in our Studdy's, especially in philosophy & ye Mathematicks which he has a fancy for. I am so full of College Accounts att prsent (being to end all my yeares concerns as Bursar this week) that I must begg yor excuse for any other: I hope I shall make good my p~miss as to yor Sons, before the next returne of ye Bearer. Wee are like to have a new Vicechancellour shortly, the Chancellours Letter being already come for Dr Marshall, Rector of Lincolne & Dean of Glocester. Our Citty, haveing much of the leaven of ye Great Citty in it, is serv'd with a Quo Warranto lately as well as it. It may possibly be as ill to digest as an Abhorrence, wch with much ado was lately sett on foot
& finish'd. 'Tis scarce gott to London yett. The 2 Terraefilij were very smart one upon another, but one of them is like to cry peccavi for lashing Dr Busby. Mr Nicholson is come into yor parts againe, I hope heel not pass by again wthout calling. Hees come for an Arch Deaconry or Chancellors place now, so that heel scarce (or rathr must not) part with ye Neice. My service to Mr William
I am Sr Yor most obleiged Freind & Servant
These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knt att Ridall-Hall. in Westmoreland. prsent.

note.value: 241. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Yours of Jun. ye 14 and June ye 21 I haue received with cloath &c for a suit and 3l~ - 2s - 6d of wch (according to your order) I gaue to my cosin Browham 2s - 6d. I haue sent by this bearer Rich. Burnyeate,
Walker's education of young Gentlemen, which cost 2s. And I haue also sent an accompt of my disburstments, which I hope will satisfie you well. I haue been at several booksellers shops, to know ye price of Humph. Prideaux's Marmora Oxoniensia, and they tell me that ye best is sold for 15s. My uncle Dalston was here lately and has enter'd his eldest son com~oner of our College. So haueing noe news worth writeing, wth my duty to your self, and my love to all my brothers and sisters I remain
For The Right worshipfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

note.value: 243. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: Although I haue not heard from you this long time, I hope you are all well, as we are here. We shall haue an election for Tabitors without question the next terme, but whether Mr Provost will be pleased to haue one or two elected is not yett certainly known: if two I shall then (being the second Senior) know my fate. It will be something chargeable if I be elected, both at ye election, and after for takeing my degree; Soe that I hope you will be pleased to send with Rich. Burnyeats mony something more than usual least I should then be too much in my Tutors bookes. We haue noe news here worth writeing, soe with my duty to your self, and my loue to all my Brothers and Sisters I remaine
For The right worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydal-hall near Kendal These

note.value: 244. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Since mine by Burnyatts July ye 27th my new prefermt has involv'd me in a peck of troubles, wch have made me longer silent than I would (or ought to have been) I know not whether you have heard of it or not, but the Corporac~on of Andover (wthin 3 miles of Weyhill) have surrendered their charter lately & have (by a surprize)
gott a clause in their new one, wch is like to spoyle my share in ye Fair, as also Mr Drakes, who is cheif Farmer to ye Hospitall of Ewelme under Dr Luff the Regius Professor of Physick in Oxon~. They design'd to have ye whole p~fitts of ye late Fair at Michaelmas, but upon a petition of ye Vicechancellors to his Maty in the behalf of ye Univrsity & College, they were forc'd to be content wth their ancient Quantum: However wee are to have a Hearing before ye King & Councill on ye 3d of ye next month, but 'tis thought theyl not stand to their determinac~on, but will desire an appeal to ye Com~on Law, where, they are told, they shall have the better: Our right & title is grounded upon prscription, & theirs on their new grant, though indeed the Fayr was held att Weyhill by ye late charter ye 41st of Eliz: yet wee can p~ve a Fair there 70 or 80 yeares before that. However since that time they have enjoy'd ye p~fitts of weights & scales & othr dues, & the Rector & ye Tenants of Ewelme Hospitall the p~fitts of ye Booths & Sheeppens. So that wee reckon our plea is good, however wee may come of. If ye bussiness should be travers'd to ye Com~on Law or Chancery, I see no reason that I should be at ye expence of ye suit, though ye College may possibly expect it, If they should, & be unwilling to continue me in my fellowship till it be decided, I am thinking of desireing to returne to my fellowship & leaveing ye Liveing (wch is about 140l~ p~ an~u~ wth out ye Fair) to some other to manage ye controvrsy, if you approve hereof. Wee shall better see what to think of things about a month hence: In ye interim all I have to add is That Dr Floyd, principall of Jesus, came in ViceChancellour on ye
6th instant, & that 3 or 4l~ will be sufficient for yor Sons use by Burnyatts.
These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knt att Rydall-hall. in Westmoreland. prsent. To be sent by ye Post to Lancaster & so to Kendall. Post pd to London 2d. 3

note.value: 246. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Since mine by ye Post on ye 8th instant (wherein I gave you a short account of the new & unexpected difficulties & troubles that were like to arise touching Wayhill Fair) I receiv'd one from you on ye 21st instant att my returne from London, (from whence I brought the inclosed, &) whither I (as also ye Provost) am like to returne again
wthin these 10 dayes, The bussiness of Wayhill Fair being to come before ye King & Councill on ye 3d of Nov: next: If it go any further Ile see what the College will do, and if theyl do nothing, Ile see what is best for me to do. I have been so hurried about of late that I am forc'd to run upon ye score wth you for yor sons Accounts, but I hope to give a faithfull Narrative thereof e're long, att least att his advancemt into an higher Sphere wch (I hope) will not be long deferr'd now. Wee expect Mr Nicholson this week, It seemes he has gott the ArchDeaconry of Carlile, and wee expect to hear of some appurtenances or incumbrances (or Nepotismo's) being an~ext to it. The conveniency of ye Bearer (my namesake) was an inducemt to write to you att prsent. I hope to write to you more fully att Burnyatt's returne, if I am in Towne then. On ye 6th instant Dr Floyd (principall of Jesus College) succeed or provost in his Vicechancellourship. Our citty of Oxon~ is gone up to London to defend their charter (as well as they are able) agt ye Quo Warranto. I did not care if Andover had one agt their new one. My service to Mr William. I am
Sr Yor much obleiged Freind & humble Servant
These. To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knt at Rydall-Hall near Kendall in Westmoreland. prsent

note.value: 248. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: Yours by the bearer with 3l~ I haue received, and according to your order, I gaue your letter to Mr Todd, and would also haue payed him for the booke he sent you, but he would not take anything for it, only desiering me to acquaint you when I write that he was very glad that you were pleased to accept of so small a present. Mr Dixon has been at London almost two weeks and is not yett come home, so that you cannot haue any accompt now from him. I shall shortly acquaint you how things are carried at the election the time being now very near. Soe haueing noe news worth writeing, hopeing that all are well with you, with my duty to yourself, and my loue to all my brothers and sisters, I ever remain
For The Right worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

note.value: 249. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
In my last by a youngman of our College, I acquainted you that I thought I should see London shortly, & I have accordingly done it twice of late, & have continued in Town (this latter time) a fortnight almost, but do not designe to stay much longer. Mr Provost, who
came up wth me, stay'd only a week, namely, till such time as the Hearing before King & Councill was over, & left me to manage it since; And I have done what I could in it, but have not quite setled it, The Case standing thus. After the bussiness was fully debated before the King & Councill by Counsell on both sides, 'Twas referr'd (by consent of both partyes) to a Tryall att Law, & recom~ended to the Ld cheif Justice North to setle an issue in a feigned action whereby the matter in controversy may be speedily try'd, & wherein the New Charter of Andover is not to be given in evidence att ye Tryall, but they are to try the validity of their old charter, & to see if it will enable them att length to remove a Fair from such ground as it has been kept upon not only since the Grant of it: (wch is 80 yeares) but also long before the sd charter. The issue is not setled as yet by my Ld cheif Justice (& consequently 'tis not knowne where the Tryall will be, sc: whether att ye Com~on pleas, or att ye next Assizes att Winchester, wch is more p~bable) but is like to be this next week, I have entrusted a Freind to look after it & to give me an account. The Bp of Lincolne & Sr Joseph Williamson are both in good health, I see them this morning: I met with Sr Christofer Philipson accidentally in Westminster Hall two dayes ago, but doubt, I shall not see him again before I leave the citty. I am
These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knt: att Rydall-Hall in Westmoreland To be sent by post to Kendall.

note.value: 250. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Missing of Burnyatts (by whom I recd 7l~ for yor Son) I writt to you from London, while I was transacting my bussiness there touching
Wayhill Fair, & gave you a short account how the Case stood & what success wee had had before ye King & Councill. Since my returne to Oxon~ I recd one from you by ye post, for which & yor good advice therein, I am very much obleiged unto you. I have not resolv'd as yet what measures to take about Wayhill, but think of judgeing according to ye assureance I am like to have of ye profitts of ye Fair continueing upon ye Glebe (wch in all p~bability I shall certainly know either the next Assizes att Winchester, or ye next Terme) and the encouragemt & assistance the College will afford me in manageing the Concerne & defraying the expence thereof. It has cost me 30l~ & upwards already, but the Provost has p~miss'd that (when I know the whole expence) the College shall assist me, & consider me either by continueing my Grace, or allowance of wood or some other equivalent. So that I know not what more to expect for ye prsent, But shall p~ceed to acquaint you wth some more welcome News, namely, with yor Sons being elected Tabiter, wch favour was conferr'd upon him on ye first of this Month, to the great joy of all his & yor well-wishers, & to the great satisfaction (I prsume) of the electors, they being all vnanimous in their Votes for him. He is to be admitted (and will I hope have his Degree too) before ye ending of ye Terme on ye 18 of this month: There were 2 more Tabitrs (besides a ffellow & a chaplain) elected wth him, sc: one Highmore (who is his Senr) & one Cannon (the provosts Serviter) who is his Junr, as also Simsons & Harrisons Junr, whereat I doubt Mr Simson of Kendall will be troubld, especially upon his Sons account: yet as farr as I can perceive neither his Son nor Harrison is to be blamed, there being nothing objected either agt their Learning or Moralls. So that wee must
resolve their missing into somthing else than their own demeritts, I will not undertake to assigne ye cause or to medle wth State affaires or ye Intrigues of a Conclave: I am satisfy'd wth yor Sons good fortune, & wish him the like the next time he appeares as a Candidate for higher promotion in Queens: for he must think of that now & endeavour to qualify himself for it. After his admission into his Tabiters place & expences of that & his Degree, I shall send you his Accounts, whereby (as also by those you have had already) youl see, or at least guess, what it has cost you to make him Tabiter & what may serve upon ye like occasion another time. Pray prsent my service to Mr William, & beleive me to be
These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knt att Rydall-Hall near Kendall in Westmoreland prsent. To be sent by post to Lancastr & Kendall

note.value: 252. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Yors dated Dec: 15th I receiv'd, together wth ye inclosed, which I deliver'd to Mr Provost att his returne to ye College two dayes ago. I was also out of Towne (sc: att Weyhill) till ye 5th instant, which occasion'd my silence thus long. And now I hope 'tis not too late, either to wish you an happy New-Year, or to acquaint you that yor son is Batchlour of Arts, as well as Tabiter, or to send you his Accounts after such long delayes. I have writt them on the other side & stated them as clearly & punctually as I could, and if there be any mistakes in them they shall be rectify'd upon the least notice, & the particular Bills shall be likewise sent if you have a mind to them. But I hope youl find nothing in them but what is moderate, & that yor son has not been extravagant. Mr Simsons son & Harrison took their Degrees at ye same time wth him, & so put themselves of ye foundation, but (before they did so) endeavours were used in ye behalf of Simson to prvail upon Mr Provost to hearken to an election for him the next Terme & to grant him (if he was elected) seniority of Cannon, (according to his standing) But he did not seem inclinable either to the one or the other. So the poor boyes must be content & dos as well as they can. I have advised Mr Simson (because I had a letter from him about his Son, wch came too late) to continue his Son in ye College till he is Master of Arts, & to lay out for prfermt
for him in the meane time, & (if he think fitt) to gett the next prsentac~on of a good Liveing for him (if he can) after some ancient Incumbent. And as for Harrison, the new Arch Deacon of Carlisle designs to be as instrumentall as he can in p~cureing ye Schoolmasters place of Carlile for him. As for my own concerns att Wayhill, when I was there lately, the Issue upon which our Triall is to be, (sign'd by my Ld cheif Justice North on ye 11th of 10ber) was sent down from London & also a Coppy thereof, wth directions how to serve the Bayliff of Andover therewith: which were accordingly put in practise on New Yeares day, wherewith the Bayliff was not well pleas'd, but prtended their Counsell was not prsent when 'twas sign'd & that 'twas not according to ye Order of King & Councill & that therefore they would prferr a new petition to his Maty: So wee expect to hear how theyl proceed. It seemes the Issue (wch is to this effect, sc: ) is not according to their mind, though it seemes according to ye Order of King & Councill, & my Ld Cheif Justice that was, apprehended it to be so: and I hope it will prove so notwithstanding their cavills. They fancy it will not do their work, (seeing they have no land upon Weyhill strictly so call'd, nor ever had any, & wee can make it appear that there was a Fair there long before their Charter, possibly longer than 'tis since) & do therefore seek for evasions, & are projecting to gett a Tryall att Barr & a Midlesex Jury, (distrusting their Neighbours) So wee must watch their motions, & look to our witts & be ready for
them agt the begin~ing of ye Terme. In ye interim, wth my respects prsented to Mr William & Mr Fletcher (wn you see him) I remain
Sr Yor much obleiged Freind & humble Servant
My duty to my Fathr. I recd his late lettr & shall write e're long.
Flemings Accounts betwixt Nov: ye 24 (80) & St Tho: day (82)

note.value: ACCOUNTS OMITTED
253. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I hope you haue received ye letter I sent by the post at Xtimas. I took my degree the last terme (wch was very chargeable to me) and how much I am behind with Mr Dixon I doe not know, but he was telling me that he would giue you an accompt of all, which perhaps you haue received already. I am now begun with rendering Aristotle and divinity, and being at a want for good divinity bookes, I would desier you to send me some in English or rather in Lattin if you haue any which you can well spair. I alsoe desier you to send me some cloth for a suite with Rich. Burnyeats for I must now (being a ranck higher then I was, and keeping better company) goe handsomer, and spend more out of pockett, be as carefull, and as thrifty as I can: But what I spend more in such things will be spaired in battels, Tutorage, and chamber which will now cost me little or nothing. Soe haueing
noe news worth writeing, with my duty to your self, and my love to all my brothers and sisters, I ever remain
I send enclosed an accompt of my disburstments. For The Right worshipfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydal-hall near Kendal.

note.value: 256. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Since my last I have recd two from you, one by Rich: Dixon on Feb: 27th: & another this morning by ye young Carrier, & haveing so
convenient an opportunity att prsent as the comeing downe of Mr Mayor of Kendall, I could not omitt sending this short answer to them both. Before I left London I found myself obleig'd to retract what I had writt to my ffather concerning my comeing into ye Country this Spring, I perceiv'd my bussiness would not give way to such a journey & must therefore deferr it to a better conveniency. I hope to see a good issue of my affair by ye midle of July, if it be lookt after & well managed in ye mean time. I think I told you in my last that wee had a hearing before my Ld Keeper on ye 17th of ffebr: & that some amendmts were made in ye Issue wch he had sign'd by ye consent of both pties, & that they had accepted of ye s~d Issue, so that nothing was wanting now to bring it to a Tryall, but an agreemt on both sides as to place & time of Tryall, whereatt it yet sticks. They are for ye Barr & a Midlesex Jury, but wee are for a Hantshire Jury whereever it is try'd. I am glad 'twas not try'd ye last Assizes, because Mr Provost met with & show'd me a paper lately (amongst Dr Pottrs paprs) touching ye valuac~on of some Liveings in Hantshire (given by the late King) & amongst ye rest of Way (now Wayhill) in the pticulars of whose firstfruits & Tenths (as they were rated 26 Hen: 8vi:) the standing of ye Fair is therein recon'd att 40s. which thing if it can be made out by ye originall Record or Book of Taxation (as ye Provost dos not doubt but it may) it will do us signall service, & possibly make out a better Title for ye College than either the Hospitall of Ewelme or the Corporac~on of Andover can prtend to: but they must know nothing of this 'till it come to the push.
Mr Provost has given ye Company time to consider what theyl do about ye charges. They have anothr thing in hand att prsent sc: Mr Nicholsons concerne, Sr Joseph haveing made it his request to ye College that he may returne to his ffellowship, & hold His ArchDeaconry & prebendary wth it, att wch they are a litle startl'd (as also att some other pticulars in Sr Josephs lettr touching ye Colledge, wch they fancy Mr Nicholson informed him in) & have sent up Mr Crostwhait as an envoy to Sr Joseph, the result of whose message wee shall know e're long. In ye mean time he may suffer bye being absent in ye North. I shall go to Weyhill before Easter. My service to Mr William & Mr Fletcher when you see him. I am
Sr Yor much obleiged Freind & humble Servt
These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knt att Rydall-hall near Kendall. in Westmoreland. prsent.

note.value: 257. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Yours of Feb. 15. I haue received, and that of March ye 1st came to my hand yesterday, and according to your order I consulted with my Mercer and Taylor about a suit, and I finde by there great bills that I cannot haue a good cloth suit here as cheap as my last was, tho' I see by Mr Simpson's note, with carraige and makeing it amounts to 3l~. Soe that I think it best way to haue it ready made from London if you can conveniently, which will certainly be of ye newest fashion, and I beliue as cheap. As concerning ye colour of
coat and waist-coat I am very indifferent, if not black, or very light wich will be too flaunting. Mr Simpson of Kendal went this morning towards Cambridge to gett a new Vicar for Kendal, receiving a letter last night concerning Mr Stanfords death. Mr Dixon is yett in ye College, nor doe I hear any thing of his goeing into ye country. Soe with my duty to your self, and my loue to all my brothers and sisters, I ever remaine

A measure of my coat; one yard wide in ye breast; one yard wide bate nail in ye waist; one yard and almost quarter long; half ell and nail long in ye sleeve; and a neck to ye coat. The breeches half yard and half quarter long. For The Right worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

note.value: 258. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Haveing writt to you by Mr Mayor of Kendall on the 11th instant in answer to yor 2 last, I have not much to add by ye Bearer, only our
hearty Thanks for yor Token, & that out of yor 7l~ I receiv'd by ye Bearer, I paid the Mercer on the 20th instant 5l~ - 15s. which clear'd all his dues till that time, & I have 20s still in my hands to be answerd to yor Son as he shall have occasion. I told you in my last, that I could not possibly visit the North so soon as I once projected, I must see the bussiness of Wayhill in a better posture before I leave it to itself. I hinted something to you in my last touching a papr Mr Provost had met wth, the originall Record whereof I have sent to enquire after in ye Remembrancers Office, & if it can be met with (as Mr Provost dos not doubt but it may) wee shall be subtle enough for the Body politick. When I have had an account from London I designe to go into Hantshire to hasten the Tryall, & if wee find the Record I shall not fear to try it where they please, if they will not be brought to our terms. It seems Mr Nicholson was this day deny'd the liberty of returning to his ffellowship notwithstanding Sr Josephs intercession, but 'tis said he recd such satisfaction from ye Messenger who went up, that he referr'd the bussiness wholly to ye Society, So his year of Grace ends tomorrow. They have not discussed my bussiness as yet. Capt Tempest of Durham has been in towne a pretty while. He came up about a Nephew of his (one Shutleworth of Yorkshire) whom he enterd fellow Com~oner of Trinity College about half a year ago, His mother came up also wth him & has continued in town wth him, but that did not hinder his falling in love wth ye president of Magdalens only daughter, to whom he was married 10 weekes ago & upwards, and now they are
to go downe to Faucett in Yorkshire wth ye Capt & his Mother (the Capts Sister) if she be able to travell this next week: The young Lady is said to be with child, though she is not 16, and he is not above 17 yeares of age. John Tredeskins Rarities are come downe from London by water. The Elaboratory (wch Some call the Knick-knackatory) is almost finish'd & ready to receive them. Dr Plot who is to be Superviser of ye Elaboratory brought them downe. My service to Mr William I am
Sr Yor much obleiged Freind & Servt

Mr Ward is come down to take possession of Skelton in Cumberland wch he has in lieu of Hampton Poyle. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knt att Rydall-hall near Kendall: in Westmoreland. prsent.

note.value: 259. HENRY BROUGHAM JUNIOR TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Since you are pleas'd to conferr that honour upon me, as to make me one of those many that stand obliged to your goodnesse, I could
not without a proof of my own ingratitude omitt this opportunity of thankfully acknowledging the many fresh tokens of your love. I doe ingenuously confesse, that when I sett pen to paper, my mind told me how mean a requitall a few bare words are, and the danger of incurring your displeasure by this my boldnesse: but when on the other side I considered that thanks are the only requital I can make; and that it was better to stand accused of presumption, then undergoe the censure of ingratitude; then I resolved to give you this trouble; wch (except your goodnesse interpose) is unpardonable. Be pleased therefore to accept, what I can only give, my humblest thanks; and beleive me to be, wt I really am
Noble Sr Yr most obliged Servant and Obedient Godson
ffor The right Worshipfull Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal nigh Kendall in Westmrland These

note.value: 264. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: I have been so much employed of late about my Law concerns, that I hope youl pardon my neglect of writeing. I return'd from London on ye 7th instant only, since wch time I recd yors dated June ye 22d, as also 5s for a Token, for wch I must thank you in the name of some others as well as myself: & ought to have done so the last returne of the Carrier Burnyatts for the Token you sent then, but it seemes the multiplicity of bussiness I had upon me, made me forgett it, as well as myself. I am att prsent also involv'd in troubles wch will obleige me to be shorter than I design'd. When I was att London I brought our bussiness to a Tryall att Winchester Assizes on ye 17th instant, & it so falls out that the Bp of Winton has his Trienniall Visitac~on att Andover that same day, & he has warn'd me to preach ye Sermon, So I have both my hands full att prsent, being to examine Wittnesses & to p~vide a Sermon agt the time. I sett forward this morning towards Wayhill, so that I have only time to subscribe my self
Sr Yor much obleiged Freind & Servt
These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Kt att Rydall-hall in Westmoreland. prsent.

note.value: 265. HENRY BROUGHAM JUNIOR TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: If the sense of my duty could not excite in me the least thought of kissing your hand with a letter; yet were I in gratitude bound not to omitt any opportunity of writing, that I might make some (though never sufficient) acknowledgments of those many favours you are pleased to bestow on me. There be some so solicitous how to quitt themselves of their obligac~ons; but yet so discourteously ungratefull, that scorning to be obliged to any, can willingly embrace a favour, but yet hate the person that conferrs it. Be assured, Sir, that I am none of that number; for the sense of your goodnesse and mine own unworthinesse doe exceed the height of expression; and I have always accounted it a great honour to stand obliged to that generosity, wch has imposed the same fate upon many others as upon my self. Accept my humble duty to yr self, & pray give my service to all my Cousins . I am
Worthy Sr Yr most dutifull Godson & humble Servant
For The Right Worshipfull Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydall nigh Kendal in Westmrland

note.value: 266. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Yours by this bearer with 5l~ and ye rest of ye things I haue received; and according to your order I gave Mr Dixon your letter, and 5s to be spent amongst ye fellows. And concerning the 5s which you mention in your letter that you doe not know what became of, Mr Dixon received which was to be spent also among ye fellows, but
he neglected to acquaint you with it. Soe haueing noe news here worth writeing, with my duty to your self and my loue to all my brothers and sisters, I ever remaine
For The right worshipfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

note.value: 267. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: Although I writ to you lately by Burnyeat (which I hope is come safe to your hand) I could not pass by soe fair an opportunity, in not troubleing this bearer with a line to you (being one Mr Teasdel our Senior Tabiter) who promised to see you, whom I desier you would make welcome. I haue had some thoughts this long time to desier you (but never durst be soe bold till now) to lett me come down this winter to see you, which would be a great ease to me, seeing in that time we undergoe soe much hardship here; and alsoe little loss that season of the year, by reason of its coldness being soe unfitt for study, and very chargeable. Soe hopeing that you will consider of it, with my duty to yourself, and my loue to all my brothers and sisters, I ever remaine
For The right worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

note.value: 268. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: I could not deny Mr Dixon aboue all others a letter to you, although I writ very lately by Mr Teasdell a Tabiter of our College, which I hope is come safe to your hands: in which I desiered you to lett me come into the country about Michaelmas to stay this next winter with you. Nor doe I much question but Mr Dixon can satisfie you what a great help it will be to me to pass over a winter, without the hardships which we alwayes undergoe here at that time of the year. We haue noe news here but Mr Dixon or Mr Rooke can acquaint you with better than I, soe that I will not now presume to trouble you with any. Soe with my duty to your self, and my loue to all my brothers and sisters, I ever remaine
For The right worshipfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydal-Hall near Kendal These.

note.value: 271. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I receiv'd yours by yor Son about 2 dayes ago, wherein though you were pleas'd to owne our visiting of you as an obligac~on, yet certainly the engagement lay on our part, & the kindnesses receiv'd ought to have been acknowledg'd by us long 'ere this, especially by me; But, I hope, youl pardon the neglect, seeing I have been employ'd in receiving of money, & in hastening to manage & look after the p~fitts of my Fair. Wee spun out our journey so long (by takeing York & Northampton in our road) that I stay'd but one night in Oxon~, after which short stay Mr Langton was so kind as to go along with me to Wayhill, where he saw sheep enough, though he had mutton litle enough at ye parsonage house. I could have afforded him more, if the 30000 sheep which stood on ye Glebe Land had been all my owne: But the sight of them did well enough seeing their standing brought in 65l~i to the Rector. The Bayliff of Andover was not well pleas'd with the sight. It seems he & his brethren will attaque us once more, So I doubt I must make the other journey to London very speedily. I recd 5s of yor Son which shall be spent upon ye company either before I go or when I returne. Yor Son is nothing in my debt. There was something due to him att the last accounts sent to you, wch he has had out since in Studdy Rent over
me. Ile advise & befreind him all I may, being obleiged thereunto upon severall accounts. I have no news to send you but that the humour of Translating Books into English goes on very much in Oxon~, Cornelius Nepos is a comeing out done by severall hands, & Erasmus's Moriae Encomium is out already.
