Some say that Moses Pit has in 3 severall Editions of ye Com~on prayr Book lately printed at Oxon~ omitted the Injunction touching the Surplice, for which he is much blamed. Some say that he is lately engaged in a project about the Cole Mines in Cornwall, wch may retard the progress of ye Atlas. My service to Mr William &c. I am
Sr. Yor much obleiged Freind & humble Servt
Mr Langton prsents his humble service to you. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Kt: att Rydall-hall near Kendall. in Westmoreland. prsent.

note.value: 272. HENRY BROUGHAM JUNIOR TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I should be a rebel to gratitude, if I were not proud of this opportunity. That your good son is pleas'd to take the trouble upon
him of presenting this to your hand, is a greater kindnesse than I can any way deserve; yet it is the least of those many favours I have received att his hands. Modesty forbids me presume to write so often; but the deep sense of my debt to you stifles it's dictates, and bids me purchase gratitude though wth the censure of presumption. I shall not trouble you with repeated acknowledgmts of your goodness to me; since it is so great as exceeds all expression; and in such a case silence is the best eloquence. Only pray satisfy my ambition so far as to honour me with the titles of
Worthy Sr Your most obedient Godson and humble Servant
For The Right Worshipfull Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal nigh Kendall in Westmrland These

note.value: 274. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I know not what apology to make for my long silence, the late cold weather is too stall a Theme: yet I can lay the blame no where else, except my absence from Oxon~ & great distance in the Country
from a Post Town. I confess I made a shift to write 2 or 3 lines to my Father in the sharp season, but 'twas upon bussiness, and for a horse, which I desired him to send me up att yor Sons returne, & to let him have the conveniency of rideing of him up: And I hope heel procure a good one, as well for my sake as yr Sons. I beleive yor Son need not hasten his returne till the weather be milder & the wayes better. I fancy he could not have been with you in a more seasonable winter, I mean, as to the prjudice & hinderance of his Studdys. His fellow Tabiters have not made much of it I fancy, except in the way of expence & charge for fire & Shoo leather. ffive of the Seniors determine this Lent, & there are 4 more of our house: besides others that are expected. The small pox abate very much in Oxon~. I return'd thither out of Hantshire & Glocestershire about a week ago. I found litle alterac~on in ye College, only Lowther the poor child was dead, & Mr Provost had been indispos'd for some time & Mr Crostwhait had had a spice of ye Gout. It seemes the Vice-Chancellour has p~hibited the Booksellrs from selling Cornelius Nepos (lately translated by severall hands) by reason of some expressions in ye preface; He
has also found fault wth another preface before the first part of Plutarchs Moralls translated by severall hands. Some ffellows of
Colleges who were wittier than they should have been att an unseasonable time of the night & are said to have droll'd the She-Innkeeper of the Mitre (who was a papist) to death, were sconced 40s for Noctivagation & forc'd to recant or ask forgiveness in congregac~on. Dr Crowther the principall of St Mary Hall was arrested in his Lodgeings upon a Writt of Rebellion out of Chancery for contempt of ye Court, in refuseing to appear, & to stand to the award of some Arbitrators, wch he consented to nominate, touching the setting of a Fine, which he & Tenant of the Corps for his prebend, could not agree upon. 'Tis said the principall of Edmund Hall, haveing gott the prsentac~on of a good Liveing, will resigne the Hall. I hear since I came to this Town that Dr Mill & Mr Tompson of Bristoll are candidates for the Deanery of Bristoll
(worth about 120l~ p~ an~u~) now vacant. I was sum~on'd up to a Hearing wch wee are to have in chancery on the 21st instant, The result whereof I shall give my father an account of, & shall deferr writeing to him till then. In ye mean time pray Give my duty to him, as also my respects to yor Sons. I am
Sr Your much obleiged Freind & Servt
These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming kt: att Rydall-Hall in Westmoreland. prsent.

note.value: 280. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I happen'd to go for Hantshire before yor last (dated March ye 8 & sent by ye Northampton Carrier) came to yor Sons hands, so it continued wth your Son till my returne from London on ye 25th instant. I design'd to returne from Wayhill prsently after Easter, but I was detain'd upon the account of a Com~ission for examinac~on of ancient Wittnesses in our cause, wch was executed ye week after Easter & held for 3 or 4 dayes, and then the Terme drawing on some occasions fell out wch drew me towards London, namely, the designe of our Advrsaries to sett aside some part of my Ld Keepers last order on Feb. ye 21st, sc: that part of it wch related to a Hantshire Jury: And they did accordingly attempt it att ye begin~ing of ye Terme, but could not prvail. So wee have forced them to concurr in strikeing a Hampshire Jury of Gentlemen, and the Tryall is to be att ye Exchequer Barr the first Wednesday in ye next Terme or on June ye 4th. I have had some terms of accom~odation offerr'd to me & the College by some of ye Corporac~on, & they would willingly (I beleive) secure half (if not more) to me or ye College, if I would desist, & leave them to contend with ye Hospitall as to their right, but this is a point that must be well weigh'd and advised upon. I have acquainted ye Provost (betwixt whom & a great part of ye ffellows there's no good undrstanding att prsent) wth ye whole p~ceedings & how the case stands. I must go over to Wayhill again some time this week So I have no time to manage (or so much as think on) any such designes or intrigues as you fancyed by yor last I might be engaged in. I have not seen Mr Langton since I was at cold Ashton (where wee lived wth
a Tenant) nor heard from him but once. He is att Bristoll att prsent wth his Relac~ons. Wee spent yor 5s Token before I went last to Wayhill, & I was desired to returne you thanks for it long 'ere this. On Thursday last the Vicechancellour admitted Mr Crostwhait into ye principality of Edmund Hall, he is also Provostplace in ye College again, & not Mr Lancaster. Mr Thomson is Dean of Bristoll after all, but there wants a new Bp still. I need not tell you by whom the late Northerne Prefermts are supply'd, or that I am
My service (I pray) to Mr William, Mr Daniel, Mr Fletcher &c. These in all 5d To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knt att Rydall-hall near Kendall. in Westmoreland. prsent.

note.value: 282. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Yours of May 14 I received of my Cosin Geo. Fletcher and was very glad to hear that all was well with you. Mr Dixon has not been in Oxon~ since yours came to my hand; but we hear that he has gott ye tryal, at which how things were carried, we haue such an imperfect account, yt I shall not trouble you with it. Mr Todd intends for ye country very shortly to be ye Bish~ of Carlile's chaplin. Mr Will~
Graham was the last week here, but he staid only three days, and soe returned to London. The differences which lately happened in or College are (I hope) composed: For Mr Crosthwaite is both Principle of St Edmond Hall, and fellow of or College, wch was for a long time deny'd him by Mr Provost and some of the fellows. I haue sent you a note of my disburstments, that you may know the better what to send, though I haue not payed all off, which I should doe very shortly, if I could, ye year ending the next week. I am behind with my Mercer for somethings which I had before I took my journey, and somethings since, almost 3l~: and I doe alsoe want now a Batchlours gown which will cost 4l~ more at ye least: And the next terme I must begin to doe my exercise towards my degree, which will be partly chargeable. Soe that I hope you will be pleased to supply me accordinly by Burnyeat, with whom I shall return a bill of particulars. Soe this with my duty to your self and my love to all my brothers and sisters is all, from
For Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

note.value: 285. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Haueing soe fit an opportunity I could not pass it by without writing, though I writ lately by the post, which I hope you received before Burnyeat left the country. I haue litle more to acquaint you withall, but that the last week at a general meeting of the trainbands in this county, on night two schollars (viz. one Willis of Christ Church Coll. Batch~. of Arts, and one Bolds of Martin Coll~. com~oner) being a little in their drink, affronting the gards, and the Earle of Abbington the Lord Leutennant of this country, was sent to the castle that night
by the Procter, and publickly expell'd the University, by the Vice-Chancellor the next day. Dr Mill of or Coll~. is lately married, and has got near 3000l~ fortune. This with my duty to your self, and loue to all my brothers and sisters, is all from
The bearer is Mr Dixon's brother.
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

note.value: 288. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Though the Bearer leaves us in a very bussy time, yet I can~ot omitt returneing you thanks for your continued kindness & bounty in sending us yor old Token, wherewith wee have not rememberd you as yet (by reason of my absence att Weyhill till the begin~ing of ye Act & now 'tis scarce over) but shall do very shortly. I have litle Newes to send you but that Mr Provost went into Wales on fryday last, & that the Vicechancellour being sick, Dr Berry (Rector of Exeter Colledge) supply'd his place this Act. He has threatend to expell the 2 Terraefilij, the latter whereof retorted upon him in ye same words when he said to him "Impono tibi silentiu~" . They both of them
p~ceeded contrary to ye Vicechancellours Deputy's order, so I know not what will become of them, though the former (sc: Mr Bell of Magdalens, the other being of Lincolne) was ingenious & very mimicall. They both of them had a fling att our new Principall, & the latter was severe upon him. The one of them made smart remarks upon Dr Plot & the Societas Curiosoru~ lately erected in Oxon~ but especially upon ye Dr for his covetousness & dodgeing wth ye world as to his History of Staffordshire. One was brought in deposeing that he met Dr Plot carrying his Knickknackatory (a Nickname for ye Elaboratory) for a Raree Show to Bristoll Fair. I leave the rest to Mr Tod of Univrsity the new Bps chaplain, whom youl see att ye Assizes. As to my own concerne I prsume my Father has acquainted you that nothwithstanding or 2 Verdicts wee are yet to have a Hearing before my Ld Keeper the next Terme, which Hearing will, as I hope, end in a Decree. Till it be over I shall deferr building & other unnecessary projects. My respects to Mr William & all with you. I am
These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Kt att Rydall-Hall near Kendal. in Westmoreland. prsent.

note.value: 292. HENRY BROUGHAM JUNIOR TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: When I reflect upon the inestimable kindness you did me in procuring my admission into the Church, and on the continued course of yr goodness to me; I am ready to sink under the deep sense of my unworthiness, as being now no more able to return yr favours, than I was then, when least able. But second thoughts tell me, yr goodness is not mercenary, and that it is most apparent there, where there's the least prospect of retaliation. Upon these grounds I build all my satisfaction; and shall content my self with barely acknowledging my debt, till other circumstances have put me in a way of making some discharge. I presume this Gentleman the Bearer is not so much a stranger to you, but that you have heard of his great meritts, and good behaviour in ye Coll: and wth all how badly they have been rewarded. The thoughts of this would disencourage me in my studys; but that I hope though I am less deserving, yet I may have more friends than he had. One of whom I hope Mr Provost will be; to whom a word from you in my behalf would do much. Pray pardon this presumption, and accept the duty of
Yr most obedient Godson & Humble Servant
To The Right Worshipfull Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal-hall near Kendal in Westmrland.

note.value: 294. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I receiv'd yors by Burnyatts, and 5s by yor Son, for the former I am solely obleig'd to you: but the Society share with me in the obligac~on for the latter: And wee all wish for an opportunity of being able to make some requiteall for all yor Tokens & kindnesses. I dare say yor Son need not have doubted of future Promotion in ye House assoon as he had been capable: But seeing he is in a fair way of haveing it elsewhere, wee must submitt to yor disposeall of him, and I wish him as good prferment (in due time) as the North can afford, & there is as good there as elsewhere, if a man can catch it, as I hope he will. You do well of thinking to continue him att ye Univrsity 3 or 4 yeares longer: It will qualify him for what you bestow upon him & what he may have, and I shall not be wanting to assist him,
what I may, while I am in the Colledge, & afterwards as often as heel do me the kindness to visitt me. I must be for London again this Terme, wee are to have a Hearing before my Ld Keeper on ye 7th of next Month, if no new motions on ye 1st Day of ye Terme deferr it, I have not been serv'd wth a Quo Warranto, though Mr Drake has, So wee know not what they drive att in divideing of us, but wee suspect the worst: yet I hope wee shall be able to deal wth them either joyntly or seperately. I have little news to send you but that the Bp of Oxon~ return'd lately from visitting the Bp of Winton, who has been much indisposed of late, but is, as he said, on ye mending hand, and that there are some Candidates for the Principality of Edmund Hall, because 'tis supposd, that the Provost will declare it vacant shortly, the 6 months being expired wch the Hall Statutes allow of for its consistency wth a Fellowship. My humble service to Sr George & Mr Fletcher wn you see them, as also to Mr William & all with you. I am
Sr Yor much obleiged Freind & Servant
These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Kt att Rydall-hall near Kendall in Westmoreland prsent

note.value: 296. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
On Munday night last I got into Oxon~ very well, and on Wednesday I received my box with the money: but I have heard
nothing yet from Rob. Harrison of Grasmere concerning my horse, so that (I fear) I shall be forced to keep the horse here till Burnyeat return. We haue had an election here lately both for Fellows and Tabiters: at which Mr Teasdal and Mr Allan Fisher was elected Fellows, and my coz. Browham and three more elected Tabiters. The commissioners appointed to examin the difference in our Coll. sat last week several days, but has not made any end. This with my duty to your self and my love to all my Brothers and Sisters. I am
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-Hall near Kendal These

note.value: 299. REV. THOMAS DIXON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Yors dated ye 15th of ye last I recd only 2 or 3 dayes ago, by reason I went to Wayhill a little before yor Son arrived at Oxon & did not returne till very lately. So I have not much news to send you. I was att ye election for Kts of ye Shire for Hantshire on ye 16 instant, wee chose my Ld Cambden (son to ye E. of Gainsborough) & my Ld Wiltshire (second son to ye Marquiss of Winchestr) And the
citty of Winton chose Roger LeStrange & one Hunsy for their Burgesses the same day. I hope my Law concerne is now almost att an end, his Maty haveing been graciously pleased to cause the Quo Warranto to be with drawne upon a Hearing (wch was the first of that kind) before him att Councill Board on ye 11 of last month & to order that his Name should not be made use of in behalf of ye Towne, but that the matter should be left to ye Law. So they moved My Ld Keeper since to grant them a new Tryall att ye Com~on Pleas Barr by a forreigne Jury, & not by a Hantshire Jury att ye Kings Bench as in a formr ordr of chancery: But upon p~useing some Records, wch his Ldship had not seen before, he refused to grant them any Tryall att all, but order'd a Hearing only before him assoon as ye course of ye Court will p~mitt. Upon wch Hearing (eithr ye next Terme or ye Terme following) wee hope to obtain a Decree, And then all affrightmts & discouragemts from looking after other momentous concerns may possibly be over. If my fathr had had Quo Warrantos & such like Law Monstrs to graple with, I fancy they would have retarded him in his late adventures. But I must think of getting a better house before I gett a Housekeeper, I have been discourseing wth Workmen & have order'd Materials to be laid in, & shall go on this Sum~er as I can spare money. I may possibly have some othr occasion for money att ye Act. So if wee can get some costs after all, theyl do us a kindness. It pass't currant in Hantshire lately that ye Bayliff of Andover was arrested att London, after he & othrs had prsented ye Address, for costs upon our account, but it was upon
some other. The stage fell downe at Andover when they p~claim'd ye King wch has been look'd upon since as an ill omen to them. Pray give my service to Mr William, & to Sr George & yor nephew Mr Henry Fletcher wn you see them. I am Sr
Yor Freind & Servt in his powr
These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Kt at Rydall Hall near Kendall in Westmoreland prsent

note.value: 302. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
About five weeks since I received a letter from you, which I answered shortly after: but I have heard nothing out of the country since then. Burnyeat being to come up shortly, I would desier you to send some money by him; for I must have a gown, cassock and sash, and also pay two quarters battles, and several other things before winter be done, which will far exceed that money which I have in my hand; therefore if you would be pleased to send £20 by him (which you were saying you would allow me yearly, besides what I have fro~ Gresmere) I will manage it so, as to be very little troublesome to you. Sir Geo. Fletcher has sent for my Coz. George into the country, who begins his journey next friday, but the reason why he sends for him so suddainly, we cannot judge. Sr Lionel Jenkins's body is brought hither on Teusday next, where he is to lay in state 2 or 3 days, and then be buried in Jesus Coll. Chappel, to which College he has left 500l p~ ann~. Sir John Lowthers brother of Lowther was ent'red in or College the last week. Mr Provost is to be elected Vice Chancellour again the next week. We have noe news here but the death of ye
Ld Keeper, and that Sr John Churchill the Maister of the Rolls is laying a dyeing. Here is lately come forth the Life of Christ written by Mr Walker, head of University Coll. in 4to price 5s. This with my duty to your self and love to all my Brothers and sisters, I am
For Sr Daniel Fleming a Member of Parliament at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

note.value: 304. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Yours of the 17th instant and also that by Burnyeat I haue received with 10l, which I am afraid will fall a little short of my necessitys; yet I shall endeavour to make it goe as far as possible: our want of an Act this year, did us not (as you suppose) any great kindeness; for what an Act would have cost in treats and such like idle expences, we were forced to pay in money to the University treasury, and College library. The life of Christ sold very well here a while at first, but being afterwards something better examined, has since been prohibited by the Vice Chancellour, for leaning too much towards Popery in several places of it. So that I sent you none down
by Burnyeat. I would have writ to you ere this, but that I was not certain of your being in London till I received your last. This with my duty to yourself I am
Since the writing hereof we had the news here of the Parliament being proroged, and not knowing where you lodged I thought this ye surest way to direct it.
For Sr Daniel Fleming a member of Parliament To be left with Mr John Nicholson At Mr Sills house in the Cloisters At Westminster. London.

note.value: 306. BISHOP SMITH OF CARLISLE TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I have recd yours by this bearer, together with Sr Jo: Vaughans Reports for wch I returne you many thanks, and will be very carefull, not onely to keep it clean, but to return it also in due time. As for ye Bearer, I will upon yor recommendation try what may be done for
him, though I think he has not deserved it either from you or me. I shall wish you a good journey, and good success at Conishead, but I can hardly think you will have the company of ye Oxford schollar thither, for he continues still very ill: I had a letter on Tuesday last from Sr George, wherein he tells me he has kept his bed ever since his coming home; eats nothing; and is already grown very weak; and that they had sent for Dr Gilpin to him. On Thursday Mr Todd went over to see him, who tells me he is so very much weakened that he is not able to walk over ye floor without 2 supporting him; that he found there not onely Dr Gilpin, but another young Doctor, one Pearson who lives at Penrith or thereabout. Yesterday my Wife and
I went over to Carlile, to make a visit to Mris Rainbow, wch occasioned the bearers stay a day longer: we dined at ye Castle with ye Governor (for so everybody stiles him) who lives and eats splendidly. With mine and my wife's humble service to yourselfe, and our true respects to all yours now with you, not forgetting the young Parson at Oxford, I remaine ever
For Sr Daniel Fleming these at Rydall.

note.value: 308. BISHOP SMITH OF CARLISLE TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I have rec'd yours, with an inclosed from Mr Farrington, for whom I have a good respect, but cannot possibly serve him upon this
occasion, being long since engaged by promise to Mr Banks to endeavor his promotion fro~ St Bees to Appleby when yt Schoole should become void, and accordingly I have now lately recom~ended him to ye Colledge (who have ye sole power of Electing) but what they will do in it I cannot tell, having not as yet rec'd any answer from them. You have heard (I perceive) of ye death of our late Deane, and within a very few days after dyed his Father in law Sr Jos: Craddock. Yesterday I rec'd the news of ye Archbp of York's being dead of ye small pox: he administerd ye Com~union on Good Friday, preached on Easter-day, and dyed on ye Sunday after. Who will succeed him is not yet known, but Father Graham has already kissed ye Kings hand for ye Deanery of Carlisle. Mr Philip Musgrave is now lying dangerously ill of ye small pox, but they begin I heare to hope well of him. I am glad to hear you are all well at Rydall, and
will be glad to see Mr Fleming here; pray tell him I rec'd his kind Letter, and return him many thanks for it. My wife gives you her service, and I am ever
The Earle of Anglesey (that great Statesman) is lately dead. For Sr Daniel Fleming these at Rydall.

note.value: 309. SIR JOHN LOWTHER OF WHITEHAVEN TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I recd yrs, with yr approbation of my setting up a Carrier betwixt Kendal & Wthaven, wch is a grt confirmation to me. I doe not expect to p~fect ye design at first, & concur with you it wil be better done by others than by ye Kendal Carrier. I hear of one Tyson near you a sufficient Man, but ye place wher it wil be best done is at Keswick, for ther is but 4 dayes time to goe & return, so ye middle way is ye best, & I hear of one Hobson there. I have writ to Dr Grey
abt it, & pray doe you advise me. Yr acct of ye Bills of Mortality is very exact for 85, I cld have wish'd ye several Moneths had been so many Years backward, for ye total of each year is al I desire, wch if cast up in ye Book as I suppose they are, is less labour than ye p~ticular Moneths of one Year, but I wil not give you a further trouble living at a distance, I wil get Dr Grey who is upon ye place to doe it for me. I have sent you a Barometer by Greenwood ye Carrier wch will be in Kendal on Wednesday next, cost thirty shillings; ye Phylosophical Transactions are Six Volumes, 4 in Oldenburgs time wch cost me 20s p~ Volume. 2 since, something cheaper, now if you have onely 7 of ye whole number I know not whether to advise you to make them up, but if 7 since Oldenburg, it were not amiss if you did. let me know yr com~ands & I shal serve you. Kebles Reports are in English 3 vol. folo. price about 50s but of no grt esteem. I am
Sr Yr most affect. Kinsman & servt

The Provost of Queens has writ me this post, yt they have remov'd Mr Banks from St Bees to Appleby, had I been acquainted with it, my temper is too well known to hinder ye Advancemt of any related to me; but after wt I have done not to be consulted in it, nor how to supply St Bees does a little trouble me, & ye more yt they say tis by my Ld Bpp of Carlisles Advice.
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal Kendal Westmerland

note.value: 311. REV. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I have not writ this long time by reason we had no news till now worth troubling you with all. I received 2s 6d from Mr Dover which you sent. The late differences in this Coll. which we all thought had been composed are now near as ill as ever: for Dr Crosthwaite has very lately appealed to the Queen, and on Thursday last Mr Provost
and Dr Mill went to London about it, but how ill ye event may be to ye Coll: is yet unknown. We have four University men who declare themselves Papists, and has lately got Protections; a coppy of which I have inclosed for you. The other day I was with Dr Hide, who is very much my friend, and I was telling him of my Ld Chancellour's promises, and he told me that he thought they signified very little, unless I could gett the promise of some one particular place, as a Prebend of Glocester which is like to fall very shortly and of some value, or some other place; for he has so many Clergy men always about him, yt some or other is still ready to catch whatever falls. With my duty to your self and love to my brothers and sisters. I am

Hen. Fleming.
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

note.value: 313. BISHOP SMITH OF CARLISLE TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I was much ashamed to return you yor printed news from Scotland (brought me by yor neighbor Mr Walker) witht so much as thanks for it, or anything of an answer to yor kind letter by him, but ye blame of it must ly upon him, not me; for his hast to be at Yanwith yt night (and it was then 6 of ye clock) would not allow me any time at all to write; nor could he be prevailed with to stay all night though I importuned him. I am sorry I could not give him any hopes of Cliburne, ye thing haveing been long since promised: though, as yet,
ye old Gentleman holds out, and possibly may do so (as I hear) for some years more.

Yor news of yor Rivall's having recd a dismissio~ was very surprizing, and I should be glad to know whether it holds or no, for I have not heard anything at all (either of it or ought else) from Hutton. I do not so much as know whether my Lady Mary be yet returned out of Yorkshire; but I am told, wn she does return, Sr Ro: Fenwick and his Lady comes with her, and intend to be our neighbours, in the Deanery at Carlisle, rather than return to Bywell.

You have heard of Mr Obadiah Walker (Master of University Coll:) his having at last declared himselfe a Romish Priest; and of his Maties having Dispensed with him and 3 other persons in Oxford to hold their places there, non obstante ye 25 and 30 Car. 2di the 1. 5. 13. 23. 27. 29. 35. Eliz. and ye 1 and 3 Jac. 1mi. He has also dispensed with one Mr Edw: Slater, Rector of Putney, non obstante ye
13. 14. 17. Car: 2di and ye 21 and 28 Hen: 8vi and ye 1. 5. 13. 14. 23. 27. 29. 35 Eliz: and ye 1. 3. 7. Jacobi.
From Oxford, Dr Mill to our Archd. writes thus -

note.value: QUOTATION OMITTED

text.p:
At Edenburgh there has been hard tugging. In their Answer to ye Kings Letter, wr they say They will go as great Lengths as their Consciences will allow ; I hear it was put to ye vote whether ye word Duty should not be made use of instead of Conscience , but tis said Conscience carried it by great Odds. We were told last week in our
London News-letter yt in all probability ye Parlt in Scotland would consent to wt ye K. had demanded of them : but on Tuesday last Bas: Fielding sent me word That the Question (after a long debate) having been put on Thursday last, whether ye Laws agt Roman Cath: should be repealed, it was carried in ye Negative by very many votes, (some say above 10 to one.)

In Ireland, they say, things go worse and worse: insomuch yt ye Protestants in many parts begin to be fearfull and jealous of their safety; and yt ye price of Lands there, from 15 or 16 years purchase, is fallen to 8.
Last week his Majesty dismissed his Prot: Chaplains at Windsor from attending at ye Ceremony of Healing, wch was performed by his Romish Priests: ye service in Latin, as in Hen. 7ths time.
I am heartily glad to hear you are well at Rydall. God long continue it. I am Sr
I pray Sr that not anything of ye News above be known to come from me.
Letters from France say ye Issue of humours wherewith King is troubled does heal up every 2 moneths, and then breaks out againe. How long he may continue thus is uncertaine.
I do not yet return yor book of ye French Persecution. For Sr Daniel Fleming these at Rydall.

note.value: 314. SIR JOHN LOWTHER OF WHITEHAVEN TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I have yrs of ye 7. 12 & 28th of May. Consequently ye Money for ye Barometer, wch you needed not have been so expeditious in, but tis yr method; I thank you for yr opinion abt ye Carrier & am satisfied none but a Kendal carrier can p~form it in 4 dayes, ye country does not cooperate wth me in it, answerable to my good Intentions, & ye Complaint I made abt ye schoolmr of St Bees was not wth out cause, after so grt charge & trouble as I had been at, especially when ther was no need of it, for had ye Bpp acquainted me, I cld have helpt him to a better Mastr than Mr Banks for Apleby, but cannot help St Bees to ye like, being limitted to a master born in ye Northern Counties, all I help is to nominate any Body for ye prsent under a Bond of Resignation, for wh I have a blank by me. There is one tho near you, if he answer ye Character I have from Queens & yt he wil accept it, may serve us without condition, & yt is one Mr Rich. Jackson who now professes Physick near Kendal, he left Queens abt a year agoe, Schollr sufficient, & if no ill habits be since contracted may serve, pray let me have yr thoughts as soon as you can & whether he wil accept it if you judge him fitt - The Phylosophical Collections
are I think onely seven & fill up ye vacancy betwixt ye 1st 12 vol: of phy: Transactions & those since continued
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal Kendal Westmrland

note.value: 316. REV. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: Yours of May ye 26th I received, and am very glad to hear that all is well with you. The Bp of Oxon~ has been for a long time so very sick, that his death has been expected dayly, and is still so weak that it's thought he cannot possiblely recover. Dr Parrott a member of Parliment for this University died this week. We have a report here of Mr Todd's s inclineing much towards Popery in several sermons which he has lately preached in the country, and yt the Bp has sometimes rebuked him for it. Burnyeat is to be here in the beginning of the next moneth, and if Mr Brathwaite has not by yt time payed the 20l I would beg of you to lay as much done till he pay it, and send it by Burnyeat. This with my duty to your self and love to all my brothers and sisters. I am
For Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal-hall near Kendal These

note.value: 317. SIR JOHN LOWTHER OF WHITEHAVEN TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I have both yrs concerning Mr Richard Jackson & am much obliged to you for them, ye inclosed will shew you how much I ought to desire him, & it wil be solely his fault if he make not a considerable
man. His schollership I doubt not off, my fears are yt he has something of ye good fellow, & yt he is not stay'd & fix'd in his temper, I wld willingly lay a foundation yt I might build upon, wch makes me so solicitous for a Master, wherin if I mistake my hopes are at an end. I wish he had accepted ye Bond of Resignation, if after he had prov'd wel, it had doubled my kindness, but I esteem'd him too much to offer it him, and as a stranger to me I durst not fill ye Place absolutely for fear of being mistaken.

So soon as I have enquired a little further I wil give him a positive answer, or if he please to goe over to Whitehaven according to ye approbation & liking they shal have of him I shal be determined. I see you have no ful knowledge of him because you take no notice of an accident abt ye time of his leaving ye Colledge, concerning a Woman, much spoke of in ye Country, but yt is past & sld not weigh, provided he be now but stayed & sober. Yr approbation of yr Barometer has tempted me to send one to Whitehaven.

And to yr former enquiry concerning ye Phylosophical collections ther were never more than seven wch you have, but ye Transactions are constantly carryed on & now make abt seven or 8 Volumes, being got to I think abt Number 190.
I am Sr Yr most humble Servt

My Ld Preston is gon for ye North & wil be at ye Assises at Carlisle, pray when you are there learn if you can upon wt prtence ye Citty claims a Toll in Cumberland where they have nothing to
doe, it disturbs all or Trade in ye West of Cumberland, & seems a very foolish prtence. My Ld Preston & Sr C Musgrave say they will enquire into it, as being not less concern'd for ye County than ye Town.

note.value: COPIES OF OTHER PEOPLE'S LETTERS OMITTED

text.p: For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydall Kendal Cumberland

note.value: 318. SIR JOHN LOWTHER OF WHITEHAVEN TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
By ye paper inclos'd in my last, yr recommendation, & a letter this Post from Mr Arch Deacon to ye same purpose, you may easily conclude I have a very good opinion of Mr Jackson, both as to his Natural and Acquired parts, to wch if he ad ye application & industry necessary to this Imploymt he may assure himself of al I can do for him: but being so studious as I am of ye advancemt of St Bees, I wil not venture on an untry'd man in that Profession, how promising soever, wthout a Bond of Resignation, wch I now mention more expressly, least I might not sufficiently have explained my self in my last. You know wt I design for yt school if ye master prove deserving, & I have offerr'd me other sort of men than Mr Banks was, ready to accept it, were they within or Qualification. The matter of ye School
stands thus, Mr Stainton Curat of St Bees, officiates at prsent as Master, but being onely put in to prvent a Lapse, is ready to resign, or to let any other execute for a Tryal & take al ye Profitts, wthout prtending to anything himself; if therefore Mr Jackson like either of these wayes, to goe over upon Tryal, or to have a new Presentation immediately under a Bond as aboue, he may have his choise, & goe over as soon as he please, Mr Tickel wil receive him, & put him into Possession of ye School, if he accept it on these terms, but whether he wil thus accept it I doubt, from an Expression in yrs, yt ther needed no no Bond in his Case, nor need he regard, unless it be his own fault, whether ther be or be not, for I know he has Abilities, if he have but Industry & application to yt sort of Imploymt I propose him wth al imaginable kindness, & shal ye more make it my Business to advance him, for accepting it on these Terms; I have writ to Mr Tickell to this effect yt he may be ready to receive him if he goe, & ye sooner ye better. I beg yr excuse for al this trouble & am
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal Kendal Westmerland.

note.value: 319. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO SIR JOHN LOWTHER OF WHITEHAVEN.

text.p:
Yours of ye 6th & 10th instant are come unto my hand; & perceiveing your being affraid of Mr Rich. Jackson's being a Good Fellow,
I enquired ye other day at Kendall of Mr Mayor, Alderman Simpson, & of some other persons, concerning ye same, who all give a good account of his sobriety, & they think he will be stay'd & fix'd if he shall meet with due encouragement. As to what you write concerning a Woman I have alsoe enquired after it, & so farr as I can discover he appears to be wronged therein. I never moved him much to give a Bond of Resignation; since such Bonds look not (as some think) very well, & by yours of ye 5th of June you did not, as I understood it, expect any from him: But since you insist thereon by your last, he is willing to be bound to you in any thing yt is reasonable, you being his sole Benefactor therein; & as to his entering Bond to any other, he hopes you'l not press him unto it. You intimate as if I knew what Mr Jackson may expect for being School-master of St Bees, wch I cannot informe him; haveing only heard by Report, yt ye Scholmasters certain Sallary there is about 24 or 30l~ p~ annum & what you have added to it I do not well remember, if you ever acquainted me therewith. Mr Jackson thinks it necessary yt Mr Stainton first Resign, yt then ye College may present him, & when as he shall have a Presentation, then he must procure a Licence from ye Bishop or Ordinary, & take ye Oaths & make ye Subscriptions, & do what else is appointed by ye Statutes of 17. Car. 2. 2, 25. Car. 2. 2. &c Divers of these
things are to be done before he can lawfully or safely teach Schole at St Bees; and as to his Bond, he will enter yt when you please, if you continue to insist thereon. The Sooner these things are dispatched ye Better, & Mr Jackson hath as great a desire to be at St Bees, as you need wish: But none can fairly advise him to make more hast thither than good speed. He is willing to make you ye sole Judge of his future actions; you being his Friend, & a Person of Honour & Knowledge; & he hopes to be able to performe what you shall expect from him. At ye next Assises I shall enquire after ye Tolls, & I beleive Sr G. F. can give you a good account thereof: for I have heard yt he hath a Copy of ye City's new Charter. I hear there was a suit between Sr Francis Radclife & Carlisle concerning concerning this Shire-Toll, & yt Sr Francis was baffled; but how I am not able to informe you, althought he, or his Council, can very well do it. I am
For Sr John Lowther Baronet these at his House in Southampton-Square London

note.value: 325. SIR JOHN LOWTHER OF WHITEHAVEN TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
That I had a very good opinion of Mr Jackson you might p~ceive by my formr & yt ye Bond of Resignation was not proposed but to
shew my p~ticular care of ye School. Bonds of this Nature are of no good repute as to ye Church, having been often turn'd to private profit, but Churchmen themselves have approv'd of this, as ye onely means to support ye School under ye circumstances it is. I am therefore wel pleased wth Mr Jackson's Complyance, ye Bond is to be given to me, but wth hopes never to make use of it: for let him be assured if he doe well, ther is nothing in my power I wil not doe for him yt I can. I have writ to Oxon~ for a new Blank nomination, wch I wil im~ediately send to Mr Tickel, who at ye same time wil take Mr Staintons resignation who now onely prvents ye lapse, & wil insert Mr Jacksons Name in ye New One & may then also take ye Bond.

I leave it to Mr Jackson when he will begin, but because Mr Stainton is very little of a Schooler, ye School suffers at prsent so if he went forthwith & executed it were best Mr S need not come in ye School afterwds but let him take his own method, - I gave you an acct of both ye Phylos. Collections & Transac: if you have anything to com~and me therin you know I am ready to serve you.

As to Carlisle prtended Toll, ye new Charter gives nothing they had not before, nor is it in ye prerogative as ye Att. Gen. owns to give a Toll but wher ther is Quid pro quo as to support & maintain some Bridge or Highway. Sr G. F. writes me he thinks ther prtences cannot extend to corn exported, but saies no more. Ye Settlemt hereof is a publick service. it can onely expose ye Corporation for vainer prtences I never heard of. I am
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydall Kendall Westmerland

note.value: 326. SIR JOHN LOWTHER OF WHITEHAVEN TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: I have had a lettr from Mr Jackson of whom I have very good hopes, & doubt not but I shal have occasion to thank you for him; I have writ to ye prsent Mastr to resign, wch assoon as it is done, Mr Jackson shal have a new Presentation, & Instructions in al things yt relate to his Place.
My Ld Preston & Sr Chr. Musgrave both told me when they come to Carlisle they wd inquire into ye Business of ye Toll pray give yr assistance therin.
The Bpp of London is to appear before ye Ecclesiastical Comrs on Monday next but we hear not his Charge.
We have yet no acct of ye takeing of Buda, I am
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Carlisle Cumberland

note.value: 329. REV. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I received of Burnyeat 20£, and according to your order have now sent by him 22 Philosophical transactions , which are all as yet printed fro~ Numbr 160: And considering ye great price of ym here (wch is 20s) besides carriage I cannot understand how they should be dearer in ye country yn here. I have also sent Dr Plots History of Staffordshire , wch is 1s dearer in sheets yn wt he promised; which makes a great many subscribers here refuse to receive yir books; not questioning but in a short time to haue ym much cheaper then 15.s 06d wch is now ye price bound. Mr Todd has been in town about 3 weeks, and gives his service to you. We haue nothing of news here; for we still want a Dean of Christ Church Coll. And tho~ ther was a report about ye Country, yt one Mr Massey of Merton Coll. was to be Dean,
yet now it is very much questioned. So hopeing all is well wth you, wth my duty to your selfe, and love to all my brothers and sisters, I am
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

note.value: 332. REV. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I being yesterday at Dr Mills chamber he gaue me this enclosed Catalogue to send you; and he also bid me acquaint you in all hast that a Collection of all the ancient English Historians are now a
printing in Oxon~, in Folio, and in Latine; whereof one volume is very lately published, and the second now in the press; and the rest will be printed with all speed im~aginable. But how many Volumes there will be is not yet known (tho~ 8 or 10 are expected) and so consequently the price neither. If you will be pleased to haue them, the Dr (who is concerned in printing them) will secure one of a sort for you: And he desiers to know your pleasure as shortly as you can lett him, least all ye first volumes should be sold. Mr Todd was adviseing me the other day to leave Oxon~, and live with ye Bishp of Carlile; but I told him, that I left all to you. This with my duty to your self, and love to all my brothers and sisters. I am
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-hall near Kendal These

note.value: 335. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO REV. HENRY FLEMING. DRAFT.

text.p: Rydal, Dec. 8. 86. - As to what you write concerning Mr Todds adviseing you to leave Oxford & to live with ye Bishop of C. I do not well understand it: For although I had rather you should live with his Lordship than any other person; yet I know not whether he would be willing thereunto; and so long as Mr Todd shall think fit to continue his Lordships Chaplaine, I fancy he will be unwilling to entertaine any other; Besides I presume yt my Lord and his Lady intend for London in February next, & how long they may be obliged to stay there cannot yet be known. Give my service and hearty thankes unto Mr Todd; for I am confident he intends you well in this Advice; & when as I shall understand it more fully, I can then better know how to advise you. Haveing the other day an occasion to look amongst some old Papers, I found ye inclosed exactly as you see it. It is all of my own hand writeing & was writ Ao 1654. This you may shew unto Mr Todd, & I hope He & you will Philosophize thereon. That I may omit no particular of moment, It was writt at London, with London Ink bought at Gray's Inn Gate, & hath been ever since kept amongst other papers, not any of which are so marked

note.value: ENCLOSURE IN 335.
CALCULATIONS OMITTED

text.p:
Writ upon ye backside of ye said Note. John Ambrose was ye last Incumbent & was presented 7 years agoe unto ye Rectory of Grasmeer in ye County of Westmerland. The Lords Com~issioners granted ye Great Seal unto one John Wallas
(who pretended a lapse when there was none) not a year agoe, who outed John Ambrose out of ye aforesaid Rectory.

note.value: 336. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO THE LORD CHANCELLOR OF ENGLAND.

text.p: Haveing acquainted my son Henry Fleming with your Lordships great kindness unto him & me in being pleased to assure me that you would take care of him & helpe him to some Ecclesiastical Preferment, and He fearing that your Lordship's Great Affaires and the many Petitioners which you dayly have with you may occasion your Lordships forgetting of him at Oxford, although Prebends & other Preferments do dayly become void; I presume to intimate ye same unto your Lordship and to desire Sr Christo. Musgrave (my good Friend & kind kinsman) sometimes to do ye like; resolveing (although I have 13 children to provide for out of a small Estate, formerly sequestered, Decimated & sold by Rebels) to acquiess chearfullie in your Lordships good pleasure & to remaine alwayes heartily
My Lord Your Lordships most humble and most obedient servant
For the Right Honble the Lord High Chancellor of England these at London.

note.value: 338. GEORGE FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Wee came safe hider. I desire you to send me Dupord upon the psalmes being a Graeke Booke as soune as you can, we beging in
it morrow, if you please, the Captens are not chosen as yeat. Sr Mr Simpson besowed upon us eader a payer of Gloues when wee came, and Ms Foward would take nothing for what we had, this Sr is all present from

note.value: 339. REV. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Yours of Decembr 8. I haue received and am not a little concerned at the knavery of the book-binder whom I intrusted about Dr Plot's History of Staffordshire. I have gott that cutt which you want and will take care to send it with Burnyeat. The paper which you sent inclosed in your last, I let Mr Todd and several well experienced in new phylosophy see; and their opinion concerning it is that too much coperas being in the ink that writ it, eat those holes in it, which is noe extraordinary, nor unusual thing. Burnyeat being to come hither shortly, I must beg of you to assist Mr Braithwait if he want anything of the 20£ then due, so that I may be sure to receive it then. We have little of news here, except that Mr Massey of Merton Coll~ was instaled Dean of Christ-church Coll~. in Christmas: And that yesterday Mr Finch son to my Lord Winchelsey and Fellow of All Souls
Coll~. was made Warden of that Coll~ by his Majesties mandat, in the place of Dr. James very lately deceased. Mr Walker published a book this morning, being Two discourses concerning the Adoration of our B. Saviour in the Holy Eucharist : which we expect will be answered by some Oxford man as shortly as possible. This with my duty to your self, and love to all my brothers and sisters, I am
For Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal-hall near Kendal These

note.value: 341. BISHOP SMITH OF CARLISLE TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I returne you many thanks for yor kind Letter by this bearer, and particularly for the copy of that you lately writt to Sr G. wch will (I believe) put him hard to it. Possibly I may hear something ere long of his sense of it, for he has sent me word that he intends to be here sometime this week. I presume you have heard of the losse lately befallen my Ld Preston, for wch I am heartily sorry. What you write of ye Parliaments being to sit in Aprill is, I believe, very uncertaine as yet, for Sr Jo: Lo: (who was pleased to give us ye honour of a visit here the last week) told me he had then newly received a Letter from Sr John of Whitehaven, acquainting him yt it was believed ye Parlt would be dissolved before that time: but of this you will be better informed when you meet with ye Judges at Lancaster.
Sr Chr. M. and his son Philip too, have been called into the closet, and though ye Report has been currant here (ever since ye coming in of the last Wednesday's Post) that Sr Chr. was outed of his place in ye Tower, yet I have cause rather to believe the contrary: for by this last Post wch came in on Saturday, Sr Chr: writt to Bas. F. and gave him an account of Mr H. Savill's being displaced & of Vice-Adm. Herbert's being turned out of all his places , yet said not a word of any such thing done to him; and by another Letter, wch Bas. recd by ye same Post from one of Sr Chr: servants, to whom he had writt to let him know how matters stood wth Sr Chr: and Phil: he is assured that all is well yet, and both Father and Son very hearty and chearfull, so that Bas. I perceive gives no credit at all to those other stories: and I am prone to believe yt Sr Chr: (being a person so very usefull and serviceable) will not be laid aside in hast, nor (consequently) my Ld Dartmouth, though it is taken for granted they are a pair of Protestant Dissenters.

I will here inclose a paper wch I recd lately from a good hand, and
wch I believe you will wonder at. Ye Persons therein mentioned have all along been the heads of ye Presbyterian Faction in the town of Newcastle, men of Estates and Interest. You need not trouble yorself to return it, for I have another Copy of it by me.

I am glad to hear yor Son Mr William keeps so much at home; hoping that by this time he has shaked off those melancholy thoughts wherewith he seemed to be troubled wn he was last here. My Wife presents her humble service to you, and we do both of us returne you our most hearty thanks for favouring us thus long wth Mris Alice's good company, wch indeed hath been so very acceptable to us, yt I assure you we are both of us troubled to part with her. Pray give our services to Mris Barbara, and ere long we hope to give her Joy; yea and to Mr Daniel too, though you say nothing of that in yor Letter. I hear my Godson is still threshing hard at it at Sedbergh: God almighty blesse him, and all yours. I am
Dear Sr Yor most faithfull Servt
For Sr Daniel Fleming these at Rydall.

note.value: 342. REV. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I haue sent you by this bearer Burnyeat Mr Walker's book and
answer, as also two other bookes, which are accounted here to be as good as any which have been lately writ. The answer to Mr Walker's book is supposed to be writ by Mr Wake chaplain to my Ld Preston: And ye Guide of Controversies by Dr Will. Sherlock. Mr Walker is now a printing Luther's life and ye History of ye Reformation . Dr Crosthwaite, Dr Hide Mr Allan Fisher &c give their humble service to you, and thanks for your token. This morning I received a letter fro~ my Brother William concerning Gresmere Church and Parsonage House, with a model of the house he designes to build,
which I like very well, if the money will finish it, and adorn the church: But I am affraid that it will fall short unless you be pleased to be assisting in wood. Soe having noe news, with my duty to your self. I am
One Mr Fisher, Fellow of our Coll~. comes into ye Country with Burnyeat whom I would desier you to make welcome. For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-hall near Kendal These

note.value: 343. REV. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Mr Garnett of Kendal and one Fallowfeild of Cokermouth takeing Oxford for their way into the Country, I could doe no less then acquaint you with what news this place affords. Mr Walker's book of the English Reformation was published very lately; of wch I have secured one for you, and design (if possible) to bind it up with its answer, which we dayly expect, and so send it you by ye first opportunity. Last Munday one Mr Farmer (a Papist) brought a Mandat from ye King to be President of St Mary Magdalene Coll~,
in the place of Dr Clarke lately deceased; but ye fellows of the Coll~. meeting yesterday, rejected the Kings mandat, and elected one Mr Huff fellow of the same College; but wt may be the consequence of it we cannot as yett think. All here are very well. This with my duty to your self and love to all my Brothers and Sisters is all fro~
For Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

note.value: 344. SIR JOHN LOWTHER OF WHITEHAVEN TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
You wil excuse this slow return to yr last, when you know I have kept my chamber 40 days wthout so much as ever stiring into ye next room, & am stil weak. I am sorry you did not see Mr Jackson when he was at Kendal, but he does extraordinary wel, his schollers dubble so yt he is almost oppress'd wth numbers. I beleive he is lately marryed to one of Mr Tickels Daughters, a widdow & a good discreet Woman fitt for Boarders. ye Bpp of Lincoln has given me some Books for ye School, & I writ to ye Bpp of Carlisle yt I hop'd we sld share wth Appleby in some of his favours, we are too remote to be Rivals, & I know he has to much goodness not to encourage my endeavours, for a grt pt of wt I doe is for ye Founders sake being unwilling a charity of an Arch Bps sld sink, as it wld have done wth out my care. pray when you see my Lord know if he recd any such letter of mine for I never had an Answer - I desire also to know wt
effect of ye late Toleration in ye Counties abt you, we have many meetings here.
The two Cheif Justices have changed their Courts, Ld C. J. Herbert now in ye Common Pleas & Mr Justice Withens has his Quietus.
Magdalen Coll~ in Oxon~ has refused ye Ks Mandamus for one nominated to be head of ye House, & chosen & install'd one of their own Election.
The ViceChancellr & University of Cambridge appear'd on Thursday before ye Ecclesiastical Comrs but adjourn'd til Wednesday next.
The K. of France's Journey to Luxemburg does give some Alarum to those pts but they hope for quiet.
I am Sr Yr most humble Servt
Young Con. Braitwait & his Lady are coming to live at Warcop. The D. of Buckingham dyed this day sennigh in Yorksh.

I heartyly wish you cld be instrumental with ye Bpp to assist Dr Wilson who is in grt Distress, any smal Living to begin wth & his Countenance, wld enable me to doe better for him herafter, I wil write to my Lord when I am a little better in health.
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydall near Kendall Westmerland

note.value: 345. GEORGE FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I have received your letter & according to your command I shall acquant you with, as well as I am able or time will permit, Sr as for our tableing it is very well, & better then many others which paye a great deal more, but we have but a little chamber, for that our wollin cloes are often throwne up & downe, for therefore wee shoul have sunthing to put them in, and as for our Master he is very cinde to us, and followes us very closely, & whilst we are at ye Schoole he allwayes imployes us with makeing versis, (whilst others are repeating) who make versis, or in sum other such like thing, and whilst we are from schole he is alwayes amongst us, with many suclike, Sr we hope that you will be pleased to send for us before it be long, but seing that is soe long two cent of I am Si I shall begg your pardon for my
scribling, and we both of us desire your blessing, which is all at present from
Your very obedient Sun to command
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydall. To be left at Mr James Simpsons-shop in Kendall These.

note.value: 346. JAMES FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: These are first to beg your pardon and blessing; and after wards to let you know, accordind to your command, that I am very well satisfied both with my schole, and my table - for in the former both my Master, and Usher are very cinde unto me; and the other, I find to my great delight in all perticulers infinightly to sirpass my expectations, but it now being but a schort time untile I hope I schall have the happines Sr to se you; I schal omit to tell you every sircumstans, then being a better opportunaty, in the mean while. I reast

note.value: 348. REV. POSTHUMUS WHARTON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I have a boy in my school who I believe would give you content, and his father comeing to town very opportunely, last Wednesday, I acquainted him with ye advantage which his son might have, if you were pleas'd to admitt him into your service; he seem'd very inclinable to imbrace soe fair an opportunity, only desires to know what service you'l pleas to expect from him, besides teaching your children, and what you'l please to allow him for his pains; I am sorry your Sonn's Landlady can take noe more; for I should be very glad of further opportunitys of shewing my readyness to serve you and acknowledging the obligations I am under soe to doe, I hope in one half years time room will be made for them, and then to receive them, of whom I will promise to take what care I can; and for my Usher (if they be soe young as to fall under his hand) I dare well promise for him too, for, I know, I am now very well furnish'd in that respect, upon which
account I think myself very happy, for much depends upon the grounding of young schollars. I am Honoured Sr
Your Worship's most obliged and most obedient Servant
This, ffor the worshipfull Sr Daniel ffleming Kt, att Rydal

note.value: 350. REV. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I received yours with 5s oke, which shall be drunk by ye fellows as soon as possible. I haue now sent you two books writ by some
Oxford hand, but his name is yett unknown: one of them is a reply to that peice of Mr Walker's which I sent you before: The other is an answer to a part of his second book intituled Church Government, Part 5. And we dayly expect an answer to the remaining part of it. I haue also sent you a Coppy of an old taxation of the Arch-Diaconary of Richmond, which you writ for: in which Arch-Diaconary their are two taxations in the Manuscript, whereas in the rest (except a very few places in the Diocess of York) there is but one. I consulted Dr Hide (who is our Library keeper) Dr Crosthwaite, and some others about these taxations, and according to their opinions the Nova taxatio was made in An~o 20 Edwardi primi; but when either of them was made for certain is unknown: I have writ in the first page of the Coppy all which I can find in the MSS relateing to the time when they were made. I haue likewise sent you Dr Burnett's Travels; a booke which
is prohibited, and of which whole impressions has been ceased: so that they are not to be mett withal. Fellows of Mag~. Coll~ are to appear tomorrow before ye Com~issioners, to justify what they alledge against Mr Farmer as reasons why they would not admit him President of the Coll~. And last week the Kg sent a mandate to the same Coll~. to stop all elections till the Com~issioners had made an end of there business. About three weeks since the Com~issioners sent for a Coppy of the statutes of this University, but there not being a Coppy which can be spared, there is one to be writ out, which will require a great time. This wth my duty to your Self, and love to all my Brothers and Sisters,
I am Your very dutyful Son
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

note.value: 352. REV. POSTHUMUS WHARTON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I am desired and indeed of myself inclin'd to petition you in behalf of a young Gentleman, whom I really think very deserving, otherwise I should blush to begg your favour for him. He was my scholar a considerable time, and went from me to St. John's in Camb: soe well furnish'd that he gave his Tutour (as I have all along been inform'd) good satisfaction, there he continued till he was Graduate,
haveing still made due improvement of his time for that I constantly received such a character of him (both as to his behaviour and industry) as I was very wel pleas'd withall; At the first election after he was capable he stood for a ffellowship, but his Interest not being able to hold up against that of his Antagonist, he fell short of his hopes in that point, though without the least stain to his own person or parts, which the other Candidate (my scholar too, and an ingenious man) did himself acquaint me with; sinc that time he hath been imploy'd in teaching a considerable School in Hartfordshire (if I mistake not) which I hope hath renderd him more fit to undertake the management of that place, and office which he is in pursuit of, and is the errand of this paper - The School of Blenkhow (Sr) whereof (I understand) your worship is a Governour, is not (I hear) yet supply'd. my humble Request to you then is that you'l please (if you be not already oblig'd) to favour this young schollar with your Interest, which if you please to grant I shall be in great hopes of his success, and doubt not but he will acquit himself soe in the imploy, as becomes him, or can easyly be expected from him; I humbly crave your Wp's pardon for the trouble and boldness of this hasty scrible, which the experience of your Goodness, and Incouragement of Learning, and the hopes I have of the young man's deserts, prompted me (though as I said in hast wch my blots will testifie) to praesent to you, with hopes of acceptance, which shall be added to the long score of your other favours, and allways most gratefully acknowleg'd, by
Honoured Sr Your Wop's most faithfull humble servt
This ffor the worshipfull Sr Daniel ffleming att Rydal wth care.

note.value: 353. REV. POSTHUMUS WHARTON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: The last week I made bold to trouble you with two lines in behalf of a young Gentleman who intended to become a Candidate for Blenkhow schoole, he hath since been in Cumberland, and there understands that the election will not be till after Martinmas, which is a Term too long for him to stay; And his concerns lying soe farr remote, he thinks it will be too long a journey for him to undertake upon an uncertainty, and therefore seems to decline all further thoughts of proceeding in this Affair, I must leave him to be guided by his own inclination in the matter, but humbly crave your Wp's pardon for my praesumption in requesting soe much trouble from you, which by the instance of some ffriends, and the hopes I had of the young man's deserts I was moved to, who am
Honoured Sr Your most obliged humble (Servant)
This ffor the Worshipfull Sr Daniel ffleming Kt att Rydal.

note.value: 354. REV. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I had writ ere this to have given you an account of the Kings reception here, but haveing then a swelling in my right hand, by reason of an accidental scratch with a nail, I could not doe it, and the Gazette haveing described it so well since that time, I doe not think it worth troubleing you with now. The Dean and Cannons of Christ-Church College are cited to appear before the Lords Com~issioners on
ye 6th of next moneth; and shortly after ye Master and some of ye fellows of University Coll~. are likewise to appear, and carry their Coll~ statutes along wth them. About a moneth agoe the King sent a letter to ye Fellows of Magdalene Coll~, to admit ye Bishop of Oxon~ their President, and ye Bp by letter (being yn indisposed) desired to be admitted by proxy; to wch ye fellows answered, yt the place was full, and so they could obey neither letter. When his Majty came hither, all the Fellows of that Coll~. were ordered to attend him; wch accordingly they did: where after the King had told them how uncivilly and undutifully they had dealt wth him, in disobeying his letters; he strictly com~anded ym to goe im~ediately to their chappel, and admit the Bishop of Oxon~ President; upon which they went directly to their Chappel; and the Senr Fellow proposeing whether they would obey ye King, and elect ye Bishop? They answer'd in their turns, they were as ready to obey his Majesty in all things that lay in their power, as any of ye rest of his Majesties subjects; but the electing the Bp of Oxon~ being directly contrary to ye Statutes, and to ye positive oaths they had sworn, they could not apprhend it in their power to obey him in this matter: Only one or two at most of the fellows then present were for obeying in this. We have not had any
book from Mr Walker's press this long time, but we daly expect something, for it's reported yt he hath 1 or 2 ready for publishing. In your last it seem'd to be your pleasure that I should come into ye Country this winter, in which I shall very willingly obey you, therefore I must beg of you to send a horse, if you can conveniently, if not I hope to gett one here. However I must desier you to send by Burnyeat 20l~, for to clear battles and other arrears, to buy a gown, cassock and other cloths fit to appear in, besides materials for a journey. I am certain less cannot doe. This with my duty to your selfe and love to all my brothers and Sisters, I remain
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-hall near Kendal These

note.value: 355. GEORGE FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I hope that ye Ovid which you writ for arriv'd safe att your hands; as for our showes which you though fit to have made hear, I formald and have received paying for them 05s - 08d, Sr I desire you
to send for us if you have leasure about the 7th of December that being the day our giving over; I hope you will be pleased to let me know what bookes you think fitting for me to bring home with me, or what other things, Sr their is hear an use that when any goes away to ye Collige, that he alwayes treats some of the cheif of his School fellows with a little ale and cakes, this I Sr let you know not being my selfe ouer desirus of but that I only might know your pleasur theirin, I rest as I ough to doe
For Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydall To be left att Mr James Simpsons-shopp in Kendall These.

note.value: 356. REV. POSTHUMUS WHARTON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Your Son's diligence I have noe reason to complain of, he hath been very observant and industrious since he came to me, but really soe much time was lost before, that his care and mine hath not yet soe fully retriev'd it as to furnish him sufficiently for the Vniversity; A little time now would be of great vse to him, and very much expedite his future progress; I have frequently observ'd what influence school-Learning hath upon men's following studies, and where it hath been lacking, seldom have the persons proved soe much as even tolerable proficients; I am almost confident that if he were continued a little longer at school neither your Worship nor himself would have occasion to repent it, one half year would now doe him more good than double the time hitherto; your younger son is likewise very carefull, which I hope may in due time help him through what difficulties he meets with, what other sonns you please to commend to
me shall with all due care be regarded, for I shall always (when I have opportunity) lay out my utmost endeavours to serve you, who am
Honoured Sr Your most humble Servt

I have often advis'd both my own nearest relations and others to continue their sonns a twelmonth after they thought of sending them to the Vniversity, which they have afterwards acknowledg'd for a kindness, and some that have refus'd the advise have found yeir mistake.
This for the Worshipfull Sr Daniel ffleming att Ridal

note.value: 358. BISHOP SMITH OF CARLISLE TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: I am glad to hear that you are all well at Rydall, and return you many thanks for the favour of Mr Harry's good company, and now of Mris Alice's, whom I must intreat you not to expect so soon as Easter, but that you will give her leave to stay as long as you can spare her; they being as heartily welcome to us here as they can be to any friends they have in ye world. The Parson gave us a very good sermon, onely he is a little bashfull in ye delivery of it, but that will wear off with a little time and practice. I find he has made good use of his time at ye University; and therefore I think you shall do well, after some little longer stay amongst his Friends (till about Whitsuntide) to give him leave to return again to Oxford, where he will now improve fast, for I have reason to believe he is a hard Student.

The Bishop of Oxford is now dead (as you will find by what I have herewth sent you) & great pitty it is he dyed not a little sooner. So is Sr Tho: Clayton also, Warden of Merton Colledge. The newsletter wch you had from Hutton has in deed a great many remarkables in it, were there any great credit to be given to it, but I find Sr G. himself has no great opinion of it; I am sure I have not, having so often found it extremely fabulous. I have sent you mine of ye same date, (wth one or two more) by comparing of wch you will know wt
value to put upon that. My wife gives you her service, and I am ever
The papers wch I have sent you by Mr Daniel containe in them all the news wch I have had by the 4 last Posts. For Sr Daniel Fleming these at. Rydall.

note.value: 360. REV. POSTHUMUS WHARTON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
In my last I gave you my full thoughts concerning your son,
that I lookt upon it as very convenient and much tending to his advantage that he should continue at school till about Xtmas next,

Since that letter one or two schollars are gone to the Vniversity (though against my mind) out of his seat, and I partly understand that 'tis some trouble to him to stay behind: I confess I always heartyly desire that my schollers should stay their full time and goe in their due order, and then I should not fear but (by God's blessing) to send them competently well qualified; but I sometimes fall short of obtaining my desires, and the consequence is their own loss. Your son hath indeed behaved himself very well since he came to me, and hath made improvement answerable to the time. I only wish that he had come sooner; your own great knowledge is more then sufficient to pass a right judgment upon him to which I humbly submit, and if you think fit to commit him again to me my utmost endeavours shal never be wanting to him nor his brothers, nor to any you shall please to commit to
Honoured Sr Your Wops most obedient Sevt
This ffor the Worshipfull Sr Daniel ffleming Kt att Rydal

note.value: 364. REV. POSTHUMUS WHARTON TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Your youngest Son here hath been indispos'd these 2 or 3 days
- your other sonns acquainting me that it was your command to them that you should be inform'd by a special messenger if any indisposition befell any of them, I writt a line or two yesterday to give you notice, but ordering the messenger to call on your son, that he might bring you an account from his own mouth how his sickness dealt with him your son (it seems) was not willing to suffer him to finish his journey but told him he was better and the next day (he hop'd) he should be perfectly sound. - This morning I find the meezles are visible upon him, soe that I hope the worst (if he keep worm, of wch I have given his Landlady a charge) will be soon over - however I thought it convenient in regard of your order to your sonns to let you understand the matter, and if you please to direct any thing for him to take your directions shall be follow'd, otherwise I shall not advise him to any physick, unless it be a gentle purge when ye distemper is over. I am in hast honoured Sr
This ffor the Worshipfull, Sr Daniel Fleming Kt att Rydal.

note.value: 365. ROGER FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I know not How or in what Language or words should I express ye sense of gratitude due to you care and tenderness you have to us and so we have need to be as careful of one of another as we can, and as for James I hope he will be well sone for ye Mesles hath almost left him, but for Dick I cannot Resolve you how he is because he is hardely come to ye hight of ym yet but as sone as I can conveniently sed I will let you hear how he is, for ye caryor comes so seldame to Kendall it's uncertaine when I shall get one sent, and for Henry he hath given us Ten shillings to pay for what we lye out, and
for Aun Aray we will get a bed for hir, but she Intends to lye whith ye maid because she lyes so near him and we will be as carefull about them as we can with Gods help so I rest

Sir if you think it fit you may send for Aun Aray within tow or three dayes for j think Dick wil be wel sone for we do not know certenly whether it is ye Mesles or not because their is very fue comt forth yet.
For Sr Daniel Fleming Thesee att Rydall.

note.value: 367. GEORGE FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: We arrived here without any danger or misfortune and before the term was over; I was by my Brother (who in all respects is kinder to me than in any wise I was able to expect, so that I am very happy in haveing him here with me) enterd of St Edmund Hall under the tutorige of the Vice Principal Mr Codrington, who is very sober, civil, diligent, and a laborious man, I have a Lector in Logick from him daily, he is accounted one of the most careful in instructing of his Pupils, Dr Mill ye Principal enterd me Commoner, because theire are here only Gentlemen Commoners, and Commoners, and by his care I have a very good Chamberfellow, he was one of them who were turned forth of Modlens. I have here sent you a Bill of my Disbursements in our journey. Many were the kindnesses that I received at my departure, of which Sr it is but fitting I should give you an account; my Brother William, my Sister Wilson, my sister Alice, & my sister Tetham each of them gave me 5 shillings; my brother Daniel gave me one, and my sister Mary gave me 2s and 6d. These Sr being all which I have at present to writ, I rest

George Fleming.
The Bill of my expenses in our journey.

note.value: CALCULATIONS OMITTED

text.p: For Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal Theses

note.value: 368. REV. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: We reached this place on ye 11th instant, and tho~ ye weather was excessive hot, yet after ye two first days traveling grew easie and pleasant. On the Friday following (with ye advice of good friends, as Dr Dixon, and some others, and by reason of the Provost's absence, who is yett in Wales) I waited on Dr Mill with your letter, who im~ediately entered my Brother Com~oner of ye Hall: I was much averse to his being entered in that quality, but the Dr laying down the little difference in charge between a Batler and a Com~oner, and weighing that with the many advantages which would necessarily attend such an admission; and with his promises to satisfy you farther in it, I was forced to submit. The Dr professes great kindness to him, and has placed him in a good chamber next to his own: he has a very civil and ingenious chamber-fellow who was lately Batch. of Arts and Demy of Magdalene Coll. His Tutor is one Mr Codrington Viceprincipal of the Hall, a man reputed to be very sober and civil, exceeding industrious, and careful of his Schollars, and I question not but he'l be as careful of him as of any. Last Satturday I had him matriculated, and so just kept that term which ended that day.

The University has got time till next Term to put yir answer to ye
Quo-warranto sent agst that part of our charter relateing to ye Printing and prohibiting bookes. Last Sunday night an express came from ye Earl of Ossery to the Vice-Chancellour to acquaint him with ye death of ye Duke of Ormond, who was our Chancellour, where upon the Vice-Chan~ called a Convocation on Munday for an election of another, and ye Earl of Ossery was elected to succeed his Grandfather: but on Tuesday a Mandate came to elect ye Chancellour of England Chancellour of ye University, which comeing too late we hope it will be of no ill consequence. Bp Gifford President of Mag~. Coll~. confirmed a great many last week in ye Coll~. Chappel where they have Mass dayly, and Sermons on Sundays. The report that was about ye breaking of ye brass eagle in that Chappel is false. That Coll~ is pretty full, and all Papists except 2 or 3. The Judges came hither
last night, and this morning they were both at Sermon in St Marys Church, but in ye Afternoon Rotherham was at a Presbiterian meeting; and ye Sheriff was at Mass. This City got a new Charter ye other day but with what alterations is not known.
This with my duty to you self I am
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal These.

note.value: 370. SIR JOHN LOWTHER OF WHITEHAVEN TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Besides a circular letter wherby I have given notice of Sr G Fs & my standing at ye next election I have also written to my more pticular friends amongst wch those of Crostwhait pish are not ye least; and as I am much obliged to you for yt grt assistance I have usually had from them so I pray, to recom~end my acknowledgmts ye more to them, yt you would please to take care of ye conveyance of ye inclos'd after you have seal'd it. I know not whether Sr George be yet return'd out of Yorkshire. I have writ him 2 letters to desire him to give such Orders to my Agents as he thinks fitt. I was in hopes to have heard
from you after ye Assises & of ye receipt of ye Barometer, wch came by Tho: Briggs abt 3 weeks agoe. I have had a late letter from Rosecastell, & am well pleased with ye hopes of seeing My Lord here, being much oblig'd to him for ye Countenance he gives or school at St Bees. The Citadel of Belgrade is taken by storm, ye Garrison 4000 al put to ye sword, ye D of Bavaria wounded in ye Assault & several grt officers slain - Six capts of ye D. of Berwicks Regimt casheir'd for refusing to admit some Irish into their Companies. I am
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal Kendal Westmerland

note.value: 371. REV. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: I have here sent you my Brother George's Account, which I am confident is as moderate, as any Batler, for the first quarter. His charges will be little or nothing more then a Batler excepting tutorage, which (if one consider how negligent Tutors generally are of such, by reason of their smal allowance) none can think it money ill spent. What books I have bought him are either such as I have not, or such as I cannot want: for I shall be very careful in laying out money for anything whatever, if I can possibly assist him otherwise. By this note you may partly judge what will be convenient to send him by Burnyeat, to supply him with fireing, pay Battles, and procure other necessarys for all winter. The Dr and his Tutor are both so careful and kind to him, that I am sure hee'l never have occasion to repent his being admitted into that house. I must likewise be a humble petitioner for myself, for some money by the carrier; for by that time that he can arrive here, the sum which I brought up with me, by buying clothes, and other conveniences, will be nearly, if not altogether exhausted; and my expences are like to be such, that less then 20l cannot defray them; yet I leave that to yourself.

Our greatest discourse here is about a Parliamt, and we dayly expect the writs. We have three candidates already for this University, viz. Mr. Finch who was sollicitour, Sr Thomas Clergis, and Dr Masters who was formerly of New College: And if no more appear
