I did designe to have sent you, according to your orders, but tom could not carry
them; Pray let us not forgett our former Acquentance. My service to every body, as every one desires the same to you
I am Your affectionate Statets Man
pra give my reverence to my Bro: Ric: and excuse me For Mr Roger Fleming These att Rydall.

note.value: 620. REV. HENRY BROUGHAM TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I hope Cous: Roger will be gott safe to Rydal long 'ere this comes, and I wish you could find him answer yr hopes, and ye time and charges expended here. But his Genius leading him some other
way, you will judge it most adviseable otherwise to bestow him. His Brother is more tractable and Studious now he is alone. In their accounts (wch I send) you will observe their battles are lower'd considerably, tho' still but too high; and I believe yr Son will own where ye fault was, yt they have hitherto been so extravagant. The debt you mentioned to be discharged is brought in at 3£. 10s. 6d; wch is so unreasonable, that I told the man that trusted them, I would never enter any Such bill in my accounts, nor so far countenance Such practices; and if he be made to wait for his money, 'tis too small a punishment for what is past, and may in great measure prevent ye like for ye future. Notwithstanding if you send it up, it shall be paid and all possible care taken to amend that fault. My Service and respects as due. I am

note.value: 623. JAMES FLEMING TO ROGER FLEMING.

text.p:
After soe long a absence, a Letter would be very acceptable; I
cannot imagine ye reason of it; yor business cannot be soe great, but you may have one hour at com~and; I would gladly be inform'd with ye news country; and what is remarkable since yor departure, is as follows; The last night, Dr Pennington & my Wourship, had ye happiness to drink a glass with Mr Bowness after ye Gates at his chamber, who drunk yor health over and over, and return'd thank for our company, and would be glad of ye same opertunity. Likewise with Mr Shirlock and Mr Washington, who were all very well rounshoulderd before we parted; Yesterday buried Mr Auxlay his wife,
whose death is very much lamented; soe has my showmaker; yett it's reported, that he makes love to Sew at ye Gray-Hound. Doctor Pudsday is marry'd, as we hear, with ye Lady Willis; Mr Willis woun ye plait in pourt-mead last Thursday, where a great many Scholars were gadered; But ye undergraduates of our house, were all welcom'd home, with an imposition of 20 distick. Quo (i?) strepit in Campo hic silet in Scholis. Jaky Brougham is here, who designs to tarry ye vacation, as we suppose. Mrs Min has an elder sister come home, who excels her, as much as Katarine; As conserning ye business with
Tom Maners, and Adam Kantwell, remains un don; I desired it to be don, who promised, yett not soe soon, least it should be ye reason of an other ingagement. This night Mr Smith jur haveing his name stopt for Mr Dayle, for absenting prayers ye Horse-Race night, carried him an epistle, which proved to be ye same with one of yours, wch you & Huchinson had translated into Greek, soe how he comes of I cannot as yett tell. Mr Huchinson is gon into ye country for a quarter of
a year. Mr Brougham finding you sessed in Tom: Burneat's rowe, asked how it came; ye Senior answered that you told Tom of it, that he might take of you as of ye rest, so Mr Brougham was well satisfied; Yett as soon as ever I heard of it, I acquainted Mr Brougham with it, and told him you were gone into ye country before Tom cam, soe presently Relton was ordered to be put on for it. The money for ye bed acquoted Noas Ark, and for The hangings, which was much less than you thought of, was spent in yor name, with those whom you intirely loved. Mrs Lauther is highly displeased at you, not for seeing her before yor journey; Which makes me affraid to visit her. Cousings ye Under Cooke is gone from ye Coll: and in his place, Mr Provist put in ye Cook's Brother. Eastgate Jinny and her comrade is latly parted, and is gon to below ye Eastgate, where she has caused several to repent of their former extravigancus; The reason of this disagreement
is, as we gather from others, ye Morbus Gallicus. John Blackman, who lived at ye Coffy House, under ye East-gate, was brought in bed ye last week, which lookt very suspicious upon her; After ye wifes had been with her a long time, not thinking her to be with child (neither would she confess it) were going home, one of them thought she heard a child cry, which made them search ye bed, at which she was forst to confess; Severall people thought it was not ye first time, that she had been in that condition; She had previded no cloose for ye child; soe censure of it, as you think fit. Great water works are making here for ye good of ye Cyty; pipes are and must be layd all over Oxon~. They are working to draw ye water from frier bacon study, wch must furnish all ye pipes, a work worth any mans
observation. All ex Aula~ Edmundi are well. Mr Bird having no news to writ, begs your pardon to ye next oppertunity. Pray pardon all falts
Dr Pennington gives his service particularly to you when you write any thing extrorny to me sent in a loose paper. For Mr Roger Fleming nigh Kendal, att Rydal By ye way of London

note.value: 624. ROGER FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: from Sum~erford bothes in Chesr. Aug. ye 25. 95. Sr

Having not heard any thing from you in all this time, makes me suppose yt my letters have miscarried, but ye reason why you have not writ, I think is, because you might expect me ere this, which I beg your pardon for so doing without your leve, but it hath been out of my power to come, which I am apt to think will be yet for some time,
for both my Cousin Swettenham and his Lady, are very unwilling to part with me till she be brought abed which is expected every day, for then he designs to give you a visite him self, which till then I desire your pardon if so be I cannot get away, which is all but my duty to you and love to my Brothers and Sisters from your
My Cousin and his Lady gives their service to you and the rest. ffor Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal near Kendal Westmld

note.value: 625. JAMES FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
What the affects of your last letter were, I have almost forgott; yett one thing I remember, which Mr Browham did not act according to (to quitt the late extraviganc's) Uppon two reasons, 1st because he had noe money in his hand, and 2ly least two quick a payment should give incouragement to a future engagement, having nothing to write he gives his service to you; I have been a little uneasy for it, by ye next I hope to see it quitted; As for linning I can dispence with it till ye next oppertunity; I should think my self in your favour to be intrusted with some money to account for, which will prove both for
your profit,and my satisfaction; its my Tutor has it I know nothing what is disburst, till he send you ye Accounts; My Bro: Geo: is very well, who is all ways ready to instruct me; My Service to all Bro: and Sisters, I am
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal nigh Kendal in Westmorland By way of London

note.value: 626. GEORGE FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I writ to my Brother Dan about 5 weeks since, but whether he hath receiv'd ye Letter or no, I know not, having not had an answer. Tom, Sr, I suppose will be with you very shortly, & therefore I must humbly beg you'l be pleased to contribute to my not only being here, but well being also; & what makes me the more ashur'd of your good affection in it, is the calling to mind a kind letter you sent me, before my leaving Oxford ye last time. The monies Sr you lett me have at my coming last to Oxon, came short of what my necessities required, & therefore hope you will now double the sum~ you then were pleased to give me. Here hath been ye greatest canvassing for a New Major, yt hath been perhaps in ye memory of man; the Candidates purses bleeding as freely (as they call it here) as ever those who stood for
Burgasses for Clithero possibly could. But what Sr makes this office to be so courted now (a place formerly rather avoided then desir'd) is the stroke it gives in ye Election of Burgasses; for whether of ye opposite parties prov'd more numerous in Freemen, in ye Election of ye Major, in in all probability would be ye like in chewsing new Par. men. The E. of Abington & my Ld Wharton are ye chief of each party, and ye E. carried ye former, as also its suppos'd he'll do ye latter. Sr Will. Trumball its said will stand for ye Univ. Sr my
Bro. James is very well, & orderly & gives his duty to you, & wee both desire Sr your blessing. I am
Sr Your most obliged & obedient Son
Our Service Sr to all our Brothers & Sisters. For Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal near Kendal in Westmerland These

note.value: 630. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO JAMES FLEMING.

text.p:
I have yours of ye 22th of ye last moneth, and I am very glad to hear that you are well. Your brother Roger is not yet come home, staying still with my Cosin Swettenham in Cheshire. He is so extravagant, the Lord onely knows what will become of him. Wilful wast, makes woful want; and debauched idle & ungodly Lives, too often occasion sad Exits. I am glad to hear that you have shaken off
some of your loose & idle comrades, that you are grown more civil, provident & studious, & that you'l be advised by your brother George & follow his Example. This will be much to your Honour, & will helpe you to preferment. My Cosin Henry Brougham is much in ye Right, not to be very quick in paying off such extravagant Ticks, least there should be more of them. I hope you'l have a care for ye Future, least you be ruined. Whilst you do well, I will do what I can for you: But if you do otherwise, you'l soon Repent it. I am sorry to hear, that you have almost forgot ye effect of my last Letter. When I was at Oxford, I used to be very careful of all my Fathers Letters; to be often reading of them; & to be very careful of obeying his commands; I also kept copyes of all my Letters to him, that I might ye better remember what I writ to him, & perform what I promised him; And in these things, & in all other things that are good, it will not be amiss for you to follow your Fathers Example. When as I am well assured that trusting you with some money will not be for your & my prejudice, as it was in your brother Rogers case, I shall then be perswaded to it. The more you study, ye less you'l spend; and by your Expences I shall ye best judge of your spending your Time. Fear God, & keep his commandments, & then all things will succeed well with you. My service to my Cosin Lowther; & all other my good Friends. The Lord bless you. I am
Yours of July 16. 95 I have & I thank you for it & ye enclosed.

note.value: 632. REV. HENRY BROUGHAM TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: Yesterday, and not before, I was informed of my Cous: George's intention to go to ye East-Indies as Chaplain to a Merchant Ship. I have examined into ye thing as impartially as I can, and discoursd Several about it; and upon ye whole I look upon it to be one of ye most unaccountable projects that ever was Set a foot, considering his circumstances. 'Tis great odds but he looses his life in ye voyage, or breaks his Constitution for ever: and besides the danger, ther is neither Interest, improvement, or reputation to be got by it, as far as I can learn. I have endeavoured to break ye neck of it as much as I can; but may have got my Self ill will thereby: but Shall willingly bear with that, so I may discharge ye love and Service I owe him as a Relation & ffriend. And as such I take ye freedom to give my opinion, that if ever you made use of your autority over a child, 'tis now that yr com~ands should take place. He's not altogether so hot upon it as before; and if I had not been kept a Stranger to it, I think it should never have gone so far. I would be very sorry to obstruct any thing that might tend to his advantage; but this I think cannot prove so. If you are of another mind, I hope you will pardon ye good intention of
Dear Sr Yr most obedient Son & Servant
Cous. James go's better on with his Work, Since his Mate left him.
To Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal near Kendal Westmrland to be sent with speed.

note.value: 634. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO REV. GEORGE FLEMING.

text.p: I was very much surprised at ye Receipt of yours of ye sixth instant, & I am very much troubled that you should think of an East-Indian Voyage, which you fancy so Pleasant, and which is realy so very dangerous & full of great hazards. I cannot give my consent to it, fearing that I shall then never see you more. I had much rather, that you should continue in ye University to improve your selfe in ye Ministry, & I doubt not but that you'l get better preferment. You'l want Books & good company abroad, & I think it will be 100. to 1. whether you'l return, and 1000 to 1. whether in such a condition as Mr Evens you mention. I beleive ye Bishop will not give you leave to be so long absente; and have a care of loseing ye Substance in catching at ye Shadow. I fancy your worthy good Friend Mr Principal will not advise you to this dangerous long Voyage, & I hope yt you'l well consider it before you Imbark therein. It is not for you to turn Trader, that was never raised in it; you are not (God be praysed) in a Desperate condition; therefore consider well of it & the Lord direct you in this & all other things; & the Lord bless you. I am

note.value: 635. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO REV. HENRY BROUGHAM.

text.p:
Yours of ye 8th instant came yesterday unto my hand, for which I returne you my most hearty thankes; and I am sure that both my son George & I are much obliged unto you for your good Advice unto him. Haveing lately received a Letter from him I writ by ye last Post: But
fearing that may miss of him, I shall here give you a copy of my Letter, which I desire you to shew him, if he be yet in Oxford.

note.value: HERE FOLLOWS 634

text.p: I hope upon his Reading of this Letter, as he will not trouble himselfe with any more thoughts of an East-Indian Voyage, or of any such Extravagant Project. It is a great Folly (to say no worse) for a hopeful young Gentleman, against his Fathers Advice & Consent to hazard his Life, where there is neither Interest, Improvement, or Reputation to be got by it. Pray tell him, I am very hopeful, that what I have writ will be enough to disswade him from such a fond undertaking; and if that will not do, I will add my com~ands thereunto. I beleive not any of his Real Friends will advise him to it, nor, I think, any of his Relations. Pray continue to Advise him, & I am glad to hear well of my son James; But as to my Son Roger, he is not yet got hither. My service to all my good Friends with you. I shall ever remaine,
Sr, Your most obliged & affectionate kinsman & servant
For Mr. Hen. Brougham at Oxon.

note.value: 637. JAMES FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Yours by Tom came to my hand, & am glad to hear that you are well; This morning my Bro: George received a letter from my Bro: Michael at London, who designs ye next week to pay us a visit, if his business will permit him; Also from my Bro: Roger in Chessire, who is very well; what he proposes to himself in liveing so long with my Coz. Swetnam, I cannot imagine; my Cuz. Brougham of late hath been very much indisposed in health. That which is most remarkable
in Coll~ & University, has been ye Canvassing for Parliamt men; For ye University Sr Wm Trumble is chosen, whome Sr Chris. Musgrave opposed; For ye City Sr Edward Naris & Thomas Rowney Esq; For supplies of any necessities I can dispence with till ye next oppertunity; My Sister Bouch sent me 5s by Tom; I desire you to return her thanks. I am
His Majesty is expected here very shortly. For Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydall These.

note.value: 638. REV. GEORGE FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Yours by Tom, & the 30£ Pounds, I have received, & shall employ it as well, & putt it as farr, as I possibly can. Here are great expectations from ye new Parliament, in which representatives for this Univ. are Sr Will. Trumbal ye P. Secret. & Mr Finch who was
a Burgess for us in ye last. In the City have been very great canvassing, but Sr Edw. Norris, & Mr Rowney (who was H. Shir. of his County about 2 years agone) are elected, and we hear that in most other places hereabouts, those yt are firme to the Ch. and Gover. are elected. I have heard some say that being Chaplain to ye H. of Com~ons is accounted a good Post, you Sr must know whether its so or no; & if it be, I do not question your interest in procuring it for me. Dr Charlot Master of Univ. Coll. hath express'd an extraordinary kindness for you; & thereupon gave me an invitation to stand this next week for a Fellow-ship there, but upon his further examining ye Statutes he found it inconsistent with any other preferment & so wee lett it sleep, and desiring your Blessing I rest
Since my writing this, I have receiv'd a letter from the Captain, who is now in London, & will be in Oxon~ shortly. The King will be hear in his way to Windsor. For Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal These.

note.value: 641. JAMES FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Upon some late discourse with Mr Brougham concerning accounts I from his words conceive him to be disgusted & consequently perhaps to designe & cause some difference between you & me; therefore I humbly present ys not to prevent & praepossess you (tho' in reason I beleive I could do't) with an opinion of my frugality, but by way of Vindication to what he shall alledge agst me. 'Tis an excellent rule which Seneca lays down that Qui statuit aliquid parte inaudita~ altera~, aequu~ licet statuerit, haud aequus fuerit ; you have abundantly showed as well yor knowledge as liking of it by your practise of it for many years; and I am better certified of yor great love & tender kindness to me than to doubt or fear a due examination of both parties before condemnation of either. It may perhaps be a groundless surmise of mine, - his great indisposition of body may (as we com~only see it does) cause that most
pernicious passion of peevishness, whence might proceed our difference in stating accounts: if otherwise it behooves me in point of com~on prudence venienti occurrere morbo : I won't endeavour to clear my self from ye imputation of being very chargeable to you, time, place, & circumstances I hope will excuse this, but for any thing of extravagancy I attest ye whole College, my former (except one) and even present account, which Mr Brougham sends impartialy to witness ye contrary. To insist more particularly upon ye last, for ye former bills are cordially examined & out of ye abundance of your fatherly kindness passed by and besid's I am more imediately concernd in this, I do with all submission offer this to your consideration, 1st ye inconveniency of ticking; for those who know before they must credit (perhaps for a pretty while) will without doubt exact, for conscience I am sure won't check those I am forc'd to deal with by Mr Broughams order: where such exaction is there must needs be large bills. 2ly ye neglect of paying & clearing accounts frequently. The more a snowball is rowled over, ye more still it contracts & grows ye larger even into a mountain: Thus a Taylor's (tho' perhaps Mr Bro: will take ye least notice of him, yet I am sure he deserves most) a shoemaker's, a glover's bill by continual addition so encreases that at last it must be cut off by yards at a time. This some in ye Vniversity have fatally experience, & this (thow agst your will) is nigh my case. I know you are for frequent & little bills, but if you examine these you'l them of a large date, and thow often by my order after a strict scrutiny brought my Tutour, yett so long as ye payment of them been deferred as to cause them to swell to such extraordinary bulk as you now see them in.

The 3d thind I shall propose to you is ye inconveniency of a partiall payment, this gives foreth opportunity's of cheating & a man that only satisfies by parcels is sure to have his goods nere a white ye cheaper. I might add ye grevances of being obliged to a particular man for his respective commodities, that whoever do's not pick, & choose his market never makes a good one, that whoever is forced to have his goods still of one man never grow's rich but on ye contrary
always poor: but I hope this will satisfie & work upon you so farr as to acquit me & take some new method of preventing with my Tutour ye like bills for ye future, wch that you may do is ye hearty desire & shall be ye utmost endeavour of
For Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydall near Kendal These By ye way of London

note.value: 645. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO REV. GEORGE FLEMING.

text.p:
I have yours of Jan. 15. 95 & I am very glad to hear yt you & your brother James are both well, which ye Lord continue: for we have a very sickly time of it in divers parts about us. Burnyates is dead, & his son will endeavour to succeed him as Carrier, in which
I wish he may have good success. Your Brother Roger came home ye week before last Xtmas, & about a week after my Cosin Swettenham came hither. He would have had Roger back again with him; but I thought he had made him a visit long enough: He is my Chaplain for ye present, & continues very orderly. Let me know, of what price, & estimation, Tanners Notitia Monastica is, you mention. Your Curate will not, I fancy, continue longer than a year, which in May next will be compleated: therefore I would have you make it your main business to fit your selfe with many good sermons, that you may then serve your Cure, according to your Duty, & which will also be for your interest: My Lord Bishop growes very old & infirm; & if you were near him, he will, I believe, be kinder unto you than at a great Distance. Your Brothers, Dan. & Michael, are gone to Rose-Castle to make his Lordship a visit, who intend to here again shortly. The Captain intends ere long to be again for London, & so for Flanders. He hath sent away about 20 volunteers, & he hopes to march away with as many more. Your Brother Daniel hath delivered me your Accompt, & seven Guineas & an half Guinea, which make 11l~i - 5s - 0d which I have sent you by this Bearer - young Tho. Burnyates. There is now no sending you any silver: for all silver money here in ye Country is much worse, than it was when you were here, and ye loss your Brother Dan. hath received of yours, by
reason good silver-money is hard to be got, the more there will be to receive fer you when milled instead of this silver grows plentiful. Although I know not how Accompts stand between my Cosin Henry Brougham & me, upon my Son James his Account, haveing not received any Letter from him concerning ye same since I sent him 30l~i, in October last, yet I have now also sent by this young Carrier six Guineas, unto you, which make nine pounds, & which I would have you pay unto my Godson, for my Son James his use, and upon my being informed how Accompts are betwixt us, I shall ye better know what Returns to make, ye next time, by this Carrier. Your sister Alice will acquaint you what things she hath sent unto you & your brother James. My best service unto Mr Principal my Godson, & unto all ye rest of my good Friends in Oxon. The Lord bless you. I am
Just now I am told, that my Lord Bishop expects you to be at Aspatrick before Easter next.

note.value: 647. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO JAMES FLEMING.

text.p: I am very glad to discover by yours of Oct. 26. 95, and by your Brother Georges since, that you are well & continues sober & studious. Your Brother Roger came hither a little before Christmas, & behaves himselfe very orderly. Be a good husband of your Money Bookes and Cloths, & follow your studies closely, and you'l reap the honour & benefit, & I the comfort of it. Your brother George will acquaint you with what money I have sent unto your Tutor for you, & I hope you'l be sure to follow their good Advice & directions. Your brother Michael will be again for the Camp. The Lord bless you. I am

note.value: 648. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO REV. HENRY BROUGHAM.

text.p: I wish that I had received yours before Tho. Burnyates had begun his Journey for Oxford, that I might have returned by him some more money unto you. I am glad to hear from you, that my son James his Deportment is civil, & that his Proficiency is answerable to ye Foundation you had to Build on; But herein give me leave to acquaint you, that I am much affraid you compliment both him & me: for his Accounts run so very high, that I much fear him to be otherwise than you represent him. I hope he'l have ye wit & grace to be directed by you; otherwise I am sure it will be much worse for him. If Tho. Burnyates could supply you with some more money, I will repay him upon his Return. The inclosed I hope you'l seal up & deliver unto my Son James. My service unto my ancient Friend your most worthy Provost, with my blessing unto both my Sons. I am
Sr, Your most obliged God-Father, & servant

note.value: 649. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO JAMES FLEMING.

text.p:
I have received your Letter, and one from your Tutor, wherein he acquaints me, that your Deportment is civil, & that your Proficiency, he hopes, is answerable to ye foundation you had to build upon. You
are much obliged unto him for his fair character, & you should not be wanting either to him or your selfe in doing chearfully what he would have you to perform for your Honour & profit & for my satisfaction. He hath sent me your Accompt, which I cannot but tell you, runs much higher than I expected, & which makes me fear, that you are not so very civil, and studious, as you are Represented. Your Battles are very high, & so are divers other things in your Accompt, especially your Mercers & Taylors Bills. Let me know ye particulars of them, & of your Stationers Bill; & I shall then be abler to make a Judgemt of ye reasonableness of them. I thought your Sister had so ordered your Linnen, as you needed not to have paid 9s - 6d for ye Altering & makeing thereof. You must be much more Frugal, or else there will be a great Fault; & you must be ordered by your Tutor in all things for your good, otherwise it will be much worse for you, & may be an hinderance to your Preferment. Be often adviseing with your Brother George, whiles he shall stay in Oxford, & the Lord bless you both. I am

note.value: 651. REV. HENRY BROUGHAM TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: I have been now a fortnight in ye Country for ye benefit of ye air, having been under a very bad state of health this half year. I recd your letters here, being but nine miles from Oxon; and this day I send ye key of my Study to have ye Bills you mention taken off ye file from amongst ye rest. Yr Son brought every bill himself to me at this last account: for I desired him so to do, being in hast, and having delayd ye matter to ye last.

By Civil deportment I meant no more than that his behaviour was Civil in his Station, and that he has not been guilty of those frolicks
and Extravagancies wch his mate heretofore Sometimes led him into. By proficiency answerable &c: I thought I could not be understood to boast: because I had acquainted you, that tho~ his ffoundation was better than his Bro~'s, yet it was far from being wt it ought to be. However, I said, I hoped we might make a shift to get a degree; and I am still in ye same mind: but truly I think he will by no means be fit for ye foundation; and if he do come upon it, he must expect nothing but Justice, for reasons you may possibly hear of hereafter. (I mean not any offence he has given himself).

There is so much confusion abt Guineas, that we can't tell wt course to take. If Money come to any Settlement, and you have ye convenience, I could wish you would make a return; because if it please God I am able to take such a Journey, I may be in ye North before ye next return of Burn:
I am Yr Dutifull & oblig'd Servt
At Midleton Stony near Bicester in Bucks~ To the Right Worshipfull Sr Dan: ffleming at Rydal near Kendal Westmd.

note.value: 653. REV. GEORGE FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Since yours by Tom, I have writt to you twice by the Post, to neither of which have I as yet receiv'd any answer; The former was to desire you to assist me with some more money, which I hope you will not refuse, now at this juncture especially, when I have lost so much by that Little I had sent; for Guines are here (& at London not so much) but at 24s, or 25s, or at most 26. The othe letter was to know whether James should now enter upon the Foundation or no; his Tutors opinion is that he is not fitt for it. The news here is about the non Subscribing members some of wch are; The Burgesses for Apulby, all ye Kts. & Burgesses for Warwickshire, except Tho.
Grey Esq~. For Oxfordshire, ye Ld. Norreys, Sr Rob. Jenkinson, Heneage Finch, Sr Edw. Norreys, Mr Rowney, James Bartie, Sr Rob. Dashwood. Sr Edw. Seymour for Totnes in Dev. ye 2 Kts. for Dorsetsh. & also for Somersetsh. Sr John Leveson Gower for
Newcastle under Lyne; ye Burgasses for ye town of Salop. & several others. Mr Taners Book Sr you writ about, is only an account of the Founders of ye Religious Houses, without any remarks upon their lives, together with the time when, & the place where. The Papists of this County are now most of them brought here to Oxford, and the Train-Bands have receiv'd orders to be ready upon the least notice. Sr I have sent you by this Bearer an Oxford Almanack, & so desiring your Blessing, rest
Sr Your most obedient son to command

Sr Charles Carterett one of ye members of ye H. of Com~ons who had refus'd to signe the Association, desir'd leave to signe the same upon Tuesday, saying he had better consider'd of it; & begged ye pardon of ye House for his refusal & he signed ye same accordingly, as all the rest have time allow'd them to do, by order of ye House till ye 10th of this month. Barnard Howard is com~itted to ye Tower, Sr
Roger L'Estrange to Newgate, & Coll. Harris & Mr Edmd. Elliat to ye Gate House. A warrant being given out against ye E. of Arran son to Dk. Hamilton he hath surrender'd himself & is under a guard at his own house. on ye 2d were taken up Ld Brudenell, Ld Ross of Ireland, Mr Hen. Burleigh, one Clifford who was a Brigadier formerly, & sent to the Tower. my Ld Peterborough being indisposed is under
confinement at his own house, & so is Sr Hen. Sheres, Sr Rich Hart one of ye members for Bristol in ye last Parl. is com~itted to ye Gate house, & Sr John Friend is in ye Custody of a Messinger wh many others.

A Messenger who was sent downe to search Sr Will. Perkins house found a great quantity of armes in an Outhouse buried under ground. some of this Sr may be newes, & I had it from a Letter writ by one of ye under Secret. For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal These.

note.value: 656. REV. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Being two nights last week at Rose to wait on the Bishop, and he and his Lady requiring me give you their Service, I thought it my
duty both in relation to you and them by the first opportunity to doe it after this manner. I have received a Letter from Brother James of the 19th instant; wherein he says that a relation of Ours & Cus. Wilson's, as he says, tho~ we have not seen him, was last week seazed and presently comitted to Ridding Goal, as one concerned in the Plott. He was taken under the name of Birkett a Kendalian, which he utterly dinys; but the name he gives out is William Herbert Collingwood . Last Thursday the Corporation of Appleby did unanimously sign the Association verbatim as it is in the Votes, and next day sent it by the Post to Sr John Lowther to present it to the King. The Bishop has likewise drawn a short Address with the Association (differing in nothing from that of the House of Com~ons, but in the word Revenge , which is left out and the sense otherwise expressed) which is to be
carried through the Diocess by the Arch-Deacon and Chancellor, and this Deanoray hath orders to meet next Friday at Appleby for that End. Sr I begg your pardon for this trouble, and leave to remain.
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-hall These.

note.value: 661. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO REV. GEORGE FLEMING.

text.p:
I am very sorry to hear, that you have had so dangerous a Fit of Sickness; and it is well that you are in good health again. Make much of ye Liveing you have, for God knowes whether I shall live, & be able, to helpe you to a better. I have ordered John Harrison of Kendal (one of my Wool-Buyers, & now at London) to return Twenty Pounds unto you, so soon as he can, for ye use of your
selfe and your Brother James. I intend shortly to send your Brother Daniel unto Aspatrick to serve you there as well as he can. Tell your Brother James, that I have seen a Letter of his unto my Son Henry, with which I am not well pleased, and that I have received James his Letter, wherein he onely writes for money, & acquaints me with Mr Saul his Death. I was in hopes, to have heard from him of his Resolving to follow his Study closely, & of his useing his utmost endeavours to get to be chosen a Poor child, as I writ formerly unto you. I hear there hath been lately an Election in Queens, but neither you nor he hath acquainted me therewith. If any of James juniors hath been elected, I shall be sorry for it, and I would know how many of ye Batlers are his Seniors, & who they are. I like not his being so long without a Tutor; and in case you and He cannot pitch upon one, then pray acquaint Mr Provost that I desire him to appoint one for my son James. I do not well understand ye Figures in ye Pedigree you sent me, as xx 13. &c. My grandson Edward Wilson dyed ye last week, & was buried upon Thursday last. The Lord fit us all for our Deaths. Let James see this Letter, I intending it to serve you both. Let me know ye date of my Letter wherein ye Promis is you mention; and then I shall give you an Answer. Old Mr Saul first heard of his Sons Death from James his Letter unto me. Your Brother James concludes his Letter unto me thus. - This I desire you to take notice of & shall expect your return. - Acquaint him, that when I was at Oxford, Sons used not thus bluntly to compliment their Fathers. The Lord bless you both. I am

note.value: 663. REV. GEORGE FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I have receiv'd a letter from you of, 26 Apr. & another since. In the former you are pleas'd to mention an order you had given John Harrison, to return us 20£, I have his bill, but ye money is not payable till ye 24th and ye party that's to pay't, being not in town untill then, I can give you no further account of it. It's true there there hath been an election in Q. Coll. but it was of Fellows whose names, if I did not give you, it was because I supposed James to have done it; (there names are Teasdale, Simpson, Gibson, & Huchinson) but
as for Poor-Children, it has not been yet, nor will as far as I can hear till about Act or Midsum~er. Mr Waugh is James's Tutor, & when I spoke to him, he was extreamly pleas'd you had made choice of him; I shall be glad to know wth whome James's money is to be intrusted. I am sorry, Sr, to hear by your last letter yt my Brother Daniel (to whom I shall alwayes be ready to make my acknowledgments) hath been put to so much trouble on my behalfe at Aspatrick, but I hope now he'll be able by your assistance, so to manage things there, as I shall not be oblig'd, to put so long a stop to my studies, as a Northcountry journey will cause. You cannot but be sensible, Sr, how great a taske ye Sac. Function is: it's reckoned great impudence to pretend to be Marster in a science in which a man's not well instructed; & if so: Alass! what's ye condition of such, as to go live upon a Cure for wch they are not duely quallified. The Learned Mr Dodwell does not as yet think himself fitt for ye Holy-function, Alass then how am I. I do not write this, Sr, out of any dislike eather to ye Pace or Function, (for I protest if I could but believe myself capable of performing ye duety requir'd, I should have saved both my self & you ye trouble of this Letter) but when in conscience I think myself to do yt better by another then by my self, I hope, none will be so hard upon me, as to use compulsion, an Argument as yet, niver thought to have ye least rellish of Xtianity, whereupon I cannot doubt of your consent to, & assistance in my being at Oxford, which I shall employ to ye best advantage & so desiring your blessing
rest Sr Your most obedt. Son.

The Pedigree Sr is as I find it in ye Mss. I have seen Dugds.
Mss of Kts. & also Vincents Mss of ye same & Anth. Woods Mss corrections of Dugd. Bar. the most material part of wch you shall have a Coppy of. Mr Kennet hath now Publish'd his Antiquities of Ambrosden in 4o. Mr Gibson is now this week gone to London to take care of ye Arch Deacons
Book wch is there now ready for the Press. For Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydall near Kendal in Westmorland These

note.value: 667. REV. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
This comes to waite on you upon a double account, both to acquaint you with my intention of going shortly to Oxford, and to request your assistance in my business there. You were first pleased to send me thither, and ingage me in takeing of Degrees, therefore I hope you'll now be pleased to help me in takeing the two last, namely Batchelor and Doctor in Divinity. It will be a chargeable undertakeing, Yet much cheaper this year than another there being noe publick Act and the assurance I have of company to contribute in part. I may save near 20l~i in leaveing Queens College, (as I am desired
to doe by a Gentleman that takes his Degrees with me) but I am loath to disgust the Provost and Fellows there, lest it prove injurious to my Brother James if he designs for the foundation: Yet I shall be constrained to do it Unless you please to supply me with some Money, it being so scarce and difficult to gett up that I cannot possibly procure enough without borrowing, which I am unwilling to doe. It's not often that I make requests to you of this nature or indeed of any, and therefore I hope to succeed. I think to be at Rydal tomorrow fortnight or in a few days after in my road, to receive Your com~ands, and in the mean time Pray give me leave to rely on Your favour, and remain
My Brother William came hither last night and I think designs for Lowther tomorrow and for Rydal some time next week. For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydale These.

note.value: 669. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO REV. JOHN WAUGH.

text.p:
I thank you for ye Favour of yours, which came but lately unto my hand. When my Letters are directed unto me at Rydal, Westmerland, then they come by ye Yorkshire Post, & are longer comeing hither; But when they are directed unto me at Rydal near Kendal, then they come much sooner by ye Lancashire Post. I am glad to hear, that you find my son James willing and tractable, hopeing by your good Advice he may dayly improve in knowledge & virtue. For his use, I have sent you ten Guinneas, as ye most payable money I can send you by this Bearer. When as my Cosin Henry Brougham's Account is settled, & I know what, & to whom to pay, I will take
care to discharge my part. My humble service to Mr Provost, & all other my kind Friends in Queens. I am
Shall we not hope for some things of ye Late Bishop of Lincolne to be published.

note.value: 670. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO REV. GEORGE FLEMING.

text.p:
I have writ unto my Lord Bishop, & I have sent your brother Daniel unto Rose & Aspatrick, who will acquaint you with what he hath done. My Lord is willing that you shall continue at Oxford longer, so as you study Divinity, & fit yourselfe for ye serveing of your cure in person, according to your Duty. Your curate is so ill to deal with, as he hath quite tyred your Brother Dan. He could not get so much payable money there as to pay Mr Overend. I have sent you ten Guineas by this Bearer for your selfe, & so much by him for Mr Waugh for ye use of James. You'l scarcely beleive how difficult it is to Receive or Pay money, that will pass. Yours of ye 5th. instant I have, & I am troubled yt your 20l~i Bill should be so ill answered. I think you had best keep ye Bill until you shall receive 20l~i of good & payable money. I have ordered your Brother Daniel to write unto Mr Harrison my wool-man; who I hope will take such course with his correspondent at London, as that you shall be well answered. I have lately received a Letter from Mr Waugh, & I have writ unto him by this Bearer. For ye rest I referr you to my last
Letter. Give my best service unto your most obligeing Principal, & unto all other my good Friends. Be often adviseing & directing of your brother James. My son Will. is now here, & I have not heard from Michael since his leaveing of London. The Lord bless you all. I am

note.value: 671. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO JAMES FLEMING.

text.p: I am very glad, that Mr Waugh, your Tutor, hath given you so good a character; and I hope you'l continue to make it good, by your prudence, civillity, & hard studying. If you shall be so unfortunate as to neglect ye present time, you'l be sure hereafter to repent it, when it will be too late: therefore be sure to imploy your precious time, as becomes a prudent & Religious man, & be not guilty of Idleing, triffleing, or Folly. Your Tutor & Brother will acquaint you with what I have sent for you. Be adviseable for your Honour & Welfare; and ye Lord bless you & preserve you out of all ill company. I am

note.value: 674. JAMES FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Yours of June ye 23 I receiv'd, not long after my Bros arrival
here, who had ye honour of a Dr grand compounder degree. Last week great expectation was here at ye Assizes to know what sentence would be pass'd of a Townsman, who kill'd a Scholar with a bottle; The Company differ'd so much in their Relation, ye Jury brought him in only guilty of Mans-Slaughter, and ye Judge com~and'd him not to keep Ale for ye future; And noe less at Winser with most of our Gentry to see ye Duke of Gloster installd. We cannot tell when to expect either admittance for ye jur Fellows or an election for poor children, which was never known to be deferd so long; Whether ye Library building occasions it or no, I cannot imagine. Which that I
may answer yor last, is ye hearty desire & shall be ye utmost endeavour of
For Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal These.

note.value: 675. GEORGE FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I receiv'd yours by the Post, but Tom is not able to answer ye contents of it; wherefore I desire some other expedient may be found out. The guines you sent me at Lent for James's use, were 2 of them laid out in exercise in ye Schools, Pocket mony's, & some other small things; the 3d was paid according to my Cosin Browhams order, & ye other three have I given Mr Waugh. James's accounts are so intricate yt we cannot do any thing with them, unless we have your assistance. For by your letters to me I am of opinion he's indebted to you about 15£ when as they make it ye contrary, for I cannot see any account given of what you sent in Octob. last, nor any
receipt of it; I suppose it was 30£; If you sent nothing then by Tom ye accounts may be right. Sr I have sent you what collections I have about ye Flemings; & Mr Lhwyd's proposals, he hath a great many Benefactors amongst wch Dr Mills is one; Dr Dixon gives his service to you. Mr Provost was not so kind to my brother, ye Dr, as might be expected, but I suppose there was no love lost. so desiring your blessing I rest
The election of poor-Children is not yet over. July 28.

Tom gave me this morning two guineas which I desire you Sr to repay, & hope you'l be pleas'd to find some way of assisting me
further, for here's no ticking, scarce for two pence, without being put in mind of it, monies are here so scarce. For Sr Daniel Fleming These.

note.value: 678. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO REV. JOHN WAUGH.

text.p:
I have Received (by Tho. Burnyates) yours of ye 28th of ye last moneth, & upon ye perusal of ye Account I find no difference, save that ye 30li sent by Burnyates unto my Cosin Brougham was not in July
95, but rather in October following. I was owing him, I beleive, 19l~i - 16s - 00d according to his Account of Febr. 1 95/6. Since which time (Feb. 6. 95) I sent to my Son Geo. F. six Guineas (then 9l~i) to be paid by him unto my Cosin Hen. Brougham, for my son James F. his use. In April following I returned by Jo. Harrison of Kendal unto my Son Geo. F. 20l~i viz. one halfe for himselfe, & ye other halfe thereof for my son James F: and in June last sent you 11l~i which you mention in your Letter, as also 3l~i - 6s - 0d received from my son Geo. F. If herein I be mistaken, it shall be rectifyed, & what shall appear due from me upon stateing of ye Account, shall be answered. I doubt not but yt you & my Son Geo. F. will so adjust this affair, as that right may be done to all parties; I thank you for your care of my son James, & I hope you'l give my service to my Ancient Friend Mr Provost, & to my other Acquaintance with you. I am,
Sr Your obliged Friend to serve you

note.value: 682. REV. GEORGE FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: I delay'd to answer yours of ye 13 of Aug. in hopes to give you at ye same time a good account of ye Election of P. Children at Queens, but that not proceeding according to our desires, it may be very proper to give you the account of ye plain matter of fact, which is this.

Upon Wednesday night last James came to my chamber, to acquaint me that orders were given to each of ye Battlers in particular, that expected to be elected poor Child~, to provide an Epistle for the Provost, according to custome; amongst these, tho' Senior, he had no notice, & so consequently not to stand; upon this he knew not what to do, but as I advised him provided his Epistle, & ye next morning gave his Tutor it to correct as the other did theirs; but his Tutor keeping ye Epistle, we heard no more of it till ye Election was over, which was upon Fryday last. Yesterday Mr Waugh came to my Chamber & express'd a great concern for what had happen'd, & said yt Mr Browham had inform'd them James was not design'd for ye
foundation; but as soon as he had receiv'd James's Epistle he went directly to ye Provost, but receiv'd no other answer then this, that he had pitch'd upon his men, tho nothing was then done, & no election till ye next day.

If I might, Sr, advise upon the matter, I am of oppinion yt its ye best to remove him from thence and that for these reasons. For 1st that what restraint the Foundation laid upon him is now taken off, whereby there's a very great temptation to idleness, if nothing else, those in his circumstances being not thought worth the takeing notice of. Again whatever his expences might be before this, dayly experience teaches us, yt after the thoughts of a Foundation are given over these constantly encrease; and it cannot be very elegable to buy a little, a very little learning (if we may compute by the progress he hath as yet made) at the expence of money's, & corruption of morrals. If he were under Dr Mill's care I do not question but we should be able to give you a much better account of him, & cure him of such things as cannot be expeted there where ye best are culpable. I should be very willing to spend some time this winter upon him, & set him in so true a light both of things here, & at Rydall, as may make him afterwards fitt to judge for himself; but you know best, Sr, what to do.

I hope, Sr, you'l please to excuse my forgetting to mention ye 10 Guines you were pleas'd to send me by Tom ye last time, & I desire you will do ye same this time, which and what I receiv'd from
your Woolman will I hope serve this winter. I hope Sr you receiv'd a letter of mine by ye Post, in which I desir'd to keep ye sum~ return'd me by a bill from Leeds, which you not contradicting my necessities oblig'd me to make use off. I shall always, Sr, make it my business, as I am very sencible it is my interest & duty, to be as gratefull as its possible; In ye Spring I shall be desirous to leave this place if you please, & and in the interim I desire your blessing & the tender of my service to all my brothers & sisters & rest
Sr Your most obliged obedient Son
Sr the Litell you mention'd in you last letter is of no moment, & I shall give you if you please a full account of it when I see you.
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal near Kendal These.

note.value: 684. JAMES FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
After what manner to give you account of my late dissappointment, least you should impulit it to my neglicence, and disrespect for ye Foundation, I hope you are satisfid; To co~ply with yor proposalls & in persuance to your orders, I previded my Epistle at ye election, thow all to noe purpose, for Mr Provest was pleas'd to admitt 5 of my jurs which was not known before; I might signifie to you ye great encouragement I have for removing to Edmond-Hall (and ye small
inducement to tarry) since ye loss of this, wch may be supply'd by my Bros instructions & example. This morning my Bro: was very well. My duty to you and love to all Bro: & Sisters, I am
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal near Kendal By way of London

note.value: 686. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO REV. JOHN WAUGH.

text.p:
Yours, & my Son's Letters comeing lately unto my hand, I was much surprised at my Son James his beeing past by at your late Election. Whatsoever may be pretended, I always designed him for ye Foundation, in case my Countrymen would think fit so far to favour him. It is true, that my Cosin Henry Brougham writt to me Feb. 26 95/96 & endeavoured to disswade me from his standing to be a Poor Child, adding these words, And if he come upon it, he must expect nothing but Justice, for Reasons you may possibly hear of hereafter, I mean not any Offence he has given himselfe . My Cosin dying soon after these Lines came to my hand, I had not ye opportunity of haveing them explained by himselfe nor have I yet heard from any others what these Reasons should be. To condemn my son without an Hearing, or me without notice of any pretended Offence, is something extraordinary, & is what one could not reasonably expect from an Ancient Friend or Acquaintance, much less from
so knowing a Body, Least my Son should be too much discouraged, I have writ to my son George to take care of his Brother, hopeing that you'l advise him therein for ye best. As concerning my Cosin Brougham's Papers, inscribed Not Entred or Omitted , if I had a copy of them, I should then acquaint you with my thoughts of them. Let me know by this Bearer what is due from my Son, & to whom, that care may be taken for the discharge thereof. I am much obliged unto you, & all others who have shewed or shall shew any kindness unto any of my Sons, or unto my selfe, & I shall remain

note.value: 687. REV. GEORGE FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I have receiv'd yours by Tom. & consulted Mr Principal & Mr Waugh, who both conclude that to remove James is the only way left to do him any good. Mr Principal is very willing to admitt him upon the conditions you mention, yt he'll be sober, civil, a good husband & governable , & will enter him how you please, but I am of oppinion that we can never do any thing with him a Batteler, who is allow'd to Battel no more than a Poor-Child of Queens, at which rate I have heard him say he could not, not to say, would not live, so yt we should be the more troubled with him, by how much the hall is stricter than Queens; & besides all our Battelers here, are such as afterwards are made servitors when a place is vacant. If a Com~oner,
the charge will be but little more, and yt is in Battels; but yet cannot Battel nigh so much as he does now at Q. & I shall take care, whilst here, to keep him within bounds; or acquaint you with it. The V. Principal is all the Tutor in the Hall except (Mr Principal) & for me to be Tutor too James would be a breach betwixt us, and for so small a time as I shall be here, Sr, will not be worth it. I say not this, Sr, to avoid any trouble, but I know his condition requiers more then one to take care of him: Mr V. P. may instruct him in Philosophy which he wants, & I shall spend the nights wth him in Gram~er & ye Classicks of which he knows little, & shall make him study the day's by me, so that if you receive not a good account of him it shall evidently his own fault.

Sr without some monies to Mr Waugh we cannot well proceed, for James owes above 12£ to the Coll. for battels, which were before the death of my Coz. Browham, and should be pay'd befor James leave ye Coll. I wish Sr you could return him 15£ for so much he wants for ye Coll. & some other expences, which he (Mr Waugh) says, Sr, you have own'd to be due to Mr Browham. Mr Waugh gives his service to you; & has explain'd yt part of Mr Browhams Letter, wch was in yours, by which he makes ye Provost, however he excuses him, the more unkind to James. Mr Browhams Letter understands by not by his own fault or such words, yt it was by the fault of my B. H. if, Sr, you think it worth ye hearing, my next shall be more cleare or rather when I come to Rydal; I desire Sr to hear as soon from you as you can, & so desiring your blessing rest

Sr I have not yet seen Tom
but receiv'd your Letter from James, & to save ye Post writ thus, not time to look it over. For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rudal near Kendal These

note.value: 688. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO REV. GEORGE FLEMING.

text.p:
I have yours of ye 14th instant; and I am much obliged unto Mr Principal, that he will be pleased to admit my son James upon ye conditions of his assureing Dr Mill, ye Vice Principal, & yourself to be sober, civil, studious, a good Husband & Governable; and if he will not do this, & perform it, I wish I had him at home, rather than he should give you all so much trouble, & be so great a charge to me, I fear, to Little, or no purpose. I am yet so in ye Dark concerning James & his Affaires, as I know not well what to direct in that matter. If you could buy him a small priced Horse, & send him hither by Tho. Burnyates, a visit here probably might do him good, & I shall then know ye better what to do. But if that be not approved of, then do with him as Mr Principal, Mr Waugh & you shall think best. You are upon ye place & may judge better of this than I can do at a distance. As to his being a com~oner, it will make higher and encrease my charge, & will I fear a little improve him; but this also I referr unto you (in case he shall not come hither) & ye nameing of his Tutor. You take no notice of your Receiving of ye Twenty Guineas I last sent (you & James) by Tho. Burnyates.
Let Mr Waugh have as much thereof as you can, & what shall remaine due to him, & ye Executor or Administrator of my Cosin Hen. B. I will take care to send by Burnyates at his next being for Oxford, (or sooner, in case I can meet with a convenient return) if in ye mean time I may have an Account of ye particulars. Let your Brother James peruse this Letter, & let him consider what Trouble (to say no more) he gives us all. My best service to your worthy Principal, & to Mr Waugh; & ye Lord bless you & James. I am

note.value: 697. REV. GEORGE FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I beg your pardon for no sooner wishing you a happy new year, & hope ye Country air has so clear'd James's eyes as yt for ye future he'll be able easily to see his own interest, & as readily embrace it. I desire you would be pleas'd when you shall think fit to return him hither, to quallify him to pay off all former scores, yt there may not be the least temptation to follow the old track. I have had several Dun~s upon his account, & Mr Waugh hath not wanted his share, but ye most importunate is Mr Browham, but of this Mr Waugh has given you account, yet has omitted in his own account, Tutorage. Supposing James, Sr, come up with ye Carrier, it will be much all one in respect of charge, how he's enter'd; For if he be Bachl in ye Vnivty Michas next then will he be Bachl in the Hall the Act before, so yt
he'll be an Vndergraduate & subject to a Tutor but just a Quarter. What monies, Sr, you send for his use (which I wish may be betwixt 15 & 20 Pounds) I shall most willingly take the charge of, & also of him if you please as Mr Prinl is now desirous I should, & shall endeavour to give you as good, or at ye worst as exact an account of both as I can.

As for my self, Sr, I am wholly at your disposal, & shall either come downe, or tarry here as you shall please to direct, & should be much more desirous of the former, had I not too to prevailing an Argumt for the latter. For haveing made use of a leaning or stooping posture when I writ or read in my study, found my self most of ye last Summer & all this Winter troubl'd by times with most violent pains in my Breast, but not in ye least imagining the reason, was so farr from omitting ye cause, yt it rather seem'd to be the only ease I had; & might have so continu'd, till ye discovery had been of no use, if Mr Principal had not one day observ'd my coat look very fresh all over excepting ye Breast where it was thread bare & so caution'd me against leaning. But besides this pain in my Breast, I alway's seem to have something sticking in my throat, which always when I read, & sometimes when I swallow is like to stifle me, & whenever of late I have attempted to do ye duty in ye Chapl have not been able to go through ye service, but forc'd to cut short or leave imperfect. Some call it a convultion, others give it harder names, but me ye hopes of being clear'd of it this spring; which makes me desirous to tarry till capable (If I may be so happy) of doing my duty in ye Country. The fears, Sr, of not being able to shake of this infirmity, & ye thoughts of wt charge & trouble I have all along & daily do put you too, are not a little damp upon my spirits, & make me one time desire to be with you, & another to try 1st what Physick can do for me; so being least able to advice for my self, as at all times, so now in particular am desirous to know your pleasure, having had frequent proof yt as you know, so you advice ye best, what's most convenient for
Sr Your most obliged & obedt Son
I desire you'l write to Mr Principal, & yt my sister send me some shirts.

I desire, Sr, whether I come down or no Mr Overend may be kept at Aspatrick; & if it be your pleasure I leave Oxon~ now, hope you'll let me know it as soon as you can, & yt you'll be pleas'd to assist me Pith 30£ to capacitate me to leave ye place as I have liv'd in it with credit. But if you think fitt to continue me here, yt may perhaps be of ye least, but I will not think of trespassing higher.
We are so in love with our Plate here, yt the old Dons make what interest I believe they can to be excus'd parting with it. Dr Barnerd Fellow formerly of St Johs Coll. died yesterday.
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydall near Kendall These

note.value: 698. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO REV. JOHN WAUGH.

text.p: Yours (sans Date) by my Son James Fleming, and your Letter of ye 11th instant by ye Post, are come unto my hand; and you should have heard from me ere this, had I known who had been my Cosin Henry Brougham's Administrator. I have returned money (notwithstanding our present confusion about money in this Country) unto my son George, for ye paying off what is due unto you from my son James; & George will, I doubt not, upon his Receiveing thereof, satisfy you, & other lawful claimers, wherein I hope you'l assist him. There is due to my two sons, Roger & James, five pounds for their Caution-money; which I hope will be allowed in their Accounts. I have ordered a Copy of my Cosin Hen. Brougham's Account to be written, which my son George will com~unicate unto you, hopeing that will give full satisfaction, & will prevent ye demanding of more than is right. In case my Cosin Jo. Brougham be his Brothers Administrator, I doubt not but all things will therein be fairly transacted, and so I hope if you be concerned therein. I thank you for all your kindnesses, & I shall ever remain
Sr Your affectionate and obliged Friend & Servant

note.value: 703. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO BISHOP SMITH OF CARLISLE.

text.p: I writ lately to my Son George at Oxford, concerning his comeing into the country, wherein I acquainted him, that I believed your Lordship & ye Parish did expect his being at Aspatrick shortly, & that I did ye same. The last Post hath brought me a Letter from Doctor Mill, my sons very kind Friend to which I know not what to answer until your Lordship shall be pleased to favour me with your Advice therein. Haveing lately congratulated Sr Joseph Williamson (my very good Friend) upon his being sworn one of His Majesties Privy Council in England, he was pleased to make me a very kind Returne, wherein your Lordship being mentioned, I have herein sent you his Letter, as also that from Doctor Mill, that your Lordship may have them both read unto you. True Friends growing fewer, I most value their kindness, therefore pray returne me the Letters inclosed by this Bearer. I am very glad to hear, by my sons Henry and James, of your Lordships good Health, & so of your Ladies. I shall heartily wish you both many happy New Yeares, & I shall ever remain,
My Lord, Your Lordships most obedient & most obliged Servant
All here are your most humble servants. For ye Bishop of Carlisle.

note.value: 704. BISHOP SMITH OF CARLISLE TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: I have yors by the bearer, and do return you my thanks for it & for yor sending me the enclos'd from Dr Mill, whch I have had read over to me with very great satisfaction, being extremely pleas'd, as I doubt not you are, wth that very good character He therein gives of yor Son George: I was alwaies willing He might have time to compleat his studies at Oxford; and upon ye Accts which ye Dr gives I shall much more readily agree to what's requested now if you will please to do so too; hoping that by Mich~s we may see Him (as is promis'd) to all our satisfacc~ons. I must thank you also for favouring me with a Sight of the L~re~ you recd from our good friend Sr Joseph Williamson, whom I think, you did well to congratulate &c. I also did the like; and I perceive He takes it very kindly from us both. I have herein, as you desire, return'd both the L~re~s, wch I hope will come safe to yor hand again & I question not will be so kept by you, as they deserve.
Mine and my wife's best Respects & Services to yor self & all yors in Ridale is all I have to add at prsent but that I am ever
Worthy Sr Yor very faithfull Servant
ffor my worthy ffriend Sr Daniel ffleming Knt, These at Ridale

note.value: 705. DR. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
The greatest news I meet withal in this Town is a List of the
Com~issioners for the Cappitation Act; who are these viz. Mr Ed. Wilson, Mr Tho. Hebblethwaite, Mr Chambre, Mr Tho. Godsalve, Mr Bird, Mr Winder, Mr Reg. Dobson, Mr Rich. Baynes, and Mr. And.
Hudleston R. General. Cousin Preston was brought to Lancaster last night and was to be buried this Day: Its said Sr Wilfrid Lawson lays claim to part of his Estate. I have just now received a Letter from Mr Matthew Rudd Schoolmaster of Ravenstondale to begg your favour in the Election for a Master at Blencow, Mr Ogle being shortly to leave that place. He has a very good character now for his learning and diligence, and may probably doe very well upon a removal: He has given Tho. Dawson another Feoffee's interest. I am

note.value: 708. REV. GEORGE FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: John Harrisons Bill of Thirty Pounds has been pay'd me very punctually; & I have pay'd off Mr Waugh and Mr Browham, as the acquits. shew; if Mr Browhams acquit. be not as it ought to be, as Mr Waugh & I scarce believe it is, we desire directions how to write a letter. Those 2 acqts., deducting five pounds caution, shew what remains in my hands; and I desire your directions what to do wth ye Bills now in my hands unpay'd, wch Mr Browham had nothing to do with.

That you have been pleas'd, Sr, upon Mr Principals request, to continue me here until Michaelmas, was what I had given over to expect, & so can esteem no less than a singular favour confer'd upon me; & therefore if I come short of your expectations, it must not be thought Mr Principals, & I hope shall not be my fault; but I know no further about his letter than that he had writt to you. I have receiv'd Sr the Fifteen Guineas you sent by Tom. & must alway's acknowledge the great charges you have been at upon my account, yet cannot think yt you'll leave me now at ye last push, which make me desire another Bill of you of 10£ by the same hands, to be pay'd me by Mr Dyson who pd~ ye last when he comes again to Oxford wch will be within this Six weeks; & be pleased to let me repay it you when I shall be in ye country, if Aspatria cannot do it sooner. I wish might have also
something to pay of Rog. & James's ticks here, 5 pounds might perhaps do so. So Sr desiring your blessing I rest
Sr your most obed~. son to com~d

Sr I give you my most hearty thanks for the Charr-Pot you was pleas'd to send me, & have dispos'd of it as directed; Mr Principal and Mr Waugh give their serve to you. Sr I have sent you an Almanack. We have nothing new now but Mr Tyrrels I. Vol. of his Engl. History which comes to ye Conquest, and is fallen into ye hands of ye Criticks who spare not to lay open all its faults.
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal. with a Book.

note.value: 712. REV. GEORGE FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
I should sooner have answer'd your last letter had I not been
desirous at ye same time to give you an account of the receipt of ye Bill you pleas'd to mention in it; but that being not yet come to my hands makes me now give over all hopes of meeting with it. I am sorry you were not then, but I hope since resolv'd of sending James up this Act, unless you think fit to bestow him some other way, then you have formerly design'd. For not to insist upon his Degree which requires his attendance here, my being now upon the place to have an eye constantly upon him, may possibly be an opportunity not again to be had, & such as may have (after this his being in ye Country) better effects upon him then any other method can be found out. I hope, Sr, you'll be pleas'd to excuse this my freedom it proceeding from no other then the desire I have to see James do well & if it should fall out otherwise it might not be in his power to blame any other then himself for it. Idleness, Sr, you know has never been though productive of any thing good, but on ye contrary ever pernicious to youth; this consideration, Sr, moves me to be the more earnest in soliciting his return, that he may be employ'd, & as he has upon your account many willing to oblige him, so he may be in a capacity to receive their favours. Once more give me leave to desire his company, yt it may not be said, yt when he was desirous to remove to a place of better instruction & example, you wear not pleas'd to consent unto it. What's due here in town from my Brothers seems all very clear except ye Chandlers Bill which Mr Waugh & I'll examine if you'll please to send money by Tom, & send you ye Bills & acquittances.

Now after my request for my Brother, be pleas'd Sr to receive one for my self. What you pleas'd to order me by Bill, not coming to me makes my necessities the greater, living now upon credit. I must therefore desire you to supply me with what you shall please to think fitting for me, to clear 2 Quarters Battles, my Hebrew Tutor, & Bottanick Professor with both wch I shall have concluded in a month or 2, add to these a new suite of clothes & other necessary expences,
to defray all these charges, Sr, will I fear require Twenty Pounds at ye least; this I hope is the last quarter I am to tarry here, & you have been all along so extraordinary kind to me, yt I cannot doubt you'll suffer me to want in this.
Mr Waugh has found by my Cos. Browham's Books that Roger & James' Caution was charg'd to you, but James's never payd to the Bousser, so that my Cos. Browham stands charg'd with it.

Mr Kennet's Book of ye Aniqties of Ambrosden was above my hands to purchase, being a 4o of 14 or 15 shillings price. If you please, Sr, to give orders how you'll have it bound, I shall take care of it. Mr. Terrils Book is in Folo price 20 shillings. Mr Principal is of oppinion its well worth your having for as much as ye Author he supposes ye best versed in Engl~. History of any man in the Kingdom. Mr Principle never read the Book. Mr Tanner is very cautious, but tould me yt he suppos'd it would not answer your expectation, & that its doubted by many whether he'll proceed or no any further; its true the Bookseller, after abut halfe of ye Book was printed off would proceed no further so yt the Author was putt to ye inconveniance of both the Charge of Printing & trouble of compiling ye work. Those who dislike the Book think he does not account right for ye Original of Govmt which is not the least part of this vol. None I meet with but grant it to contain severall good things, nor any undertake to vindicate it from a great many faults. So Sr Desiring your Blessing rest
Sr Your most obed~t Son to com~and
For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal near Kendal These

note.value: 718. REV. GEORGE FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: I receiv'd yours of ye 6th together with my Brother Daniels ye last night, & being desirous to give you ye news of this place by ye 1st Post, went directly to enquire for Dyson ye Carrier but found he was not as yn come to Oxford. Mr Teasdel one of ye Fellows of Qs Coll: came to town a few days agoe not to say weeks (after amost a years being in ye North, & a little at London) & died yesterday in ye afternoon of a Fever. Mr Dale another of ye Fellows is under ye same distemper, & by ye generallity given for lost. The former is much lamented by all yt knew him, & this will be by ye admirers of good Discipline to whom Qs was indebted for what it had. These, Sr, had nothing extrordinary in their distemper, but being upon this malencoly subject, I cannot pass by ye death of Mr Harding which had somthing singurlar in it; he was one of ye senior Fell. of Trin. Coll. Bach. of Divty a Great Tutor & of the 1st rank for Learning, & little inferior in years; this Gent having been too free with a Doctor of Physs reputation of his own Coll. was putt in ye Vice Chanl Court for it, & finding himself in danger of Beggin Pardon was so inrag'd at it, yt a sickness of 2 or 3 day's put a period to his life. he refus'd to see ye Gent whom he had wrong'd, & so became lamented of none but censer'd by most, So, Sr, begging your blessing I rest
Sr Your most obedient son to command

Sr fearing to miss ye Post, I shall answer ye rest of
your letter when I have seen Dyson. I desire you would please to consider how I may send my Bookes ye Best & Cheapest. For Sr Daniel Fleming These.

note.value: 722. SIR DANIEL FLEMING TO REV. GEORGE FLEMING.

text.p:
I have Received your Letters of Aug. 13 & of Sept. 1. 97; & I am glad to hear that you are well, & that you have Received ye 14l~i from Dyson. The best & cheapest way, I think, to send all your & your Brothers Bookes & other things hither will be to send them by your Oxford waggon unto London (in Dale-Boxes, or rather made up in a Pack) with this Direction viz. For Mr Thomas Brathwait at Kendal, to be left with Mr John Gowling at the Castle-Inn in Wood-street, London, to be sent by Kendal-Carrier. Do not mention your own name in ye Directions: for then they will come hither, as Merchants Goods, much cheaper. Thomas Brathwait aforesaid hopes to be at London about ye end of the next week, where he intends to stay about a Fourthnight; and if you can get all ye things sent unto London in that time, he will take care of them, pay for their Carryage, & send them hither; otherwise he will speak to Mr Jo. Gowling to do it for him. I hear Tho. Burnyate will begin his Journey for Oxford ye last of this moneth, by whom I shall write further, & send you more money. As concerning ye Discharging of your Brothers old Ticks, I must refer you to my Letter of ye First of July last. I like Mr Kennets Parochial Antiquities so well, as I should be glad to hear
of his Publishing his second Part, & of his improving ye History of ye Baronage of England, or ye Monasticon Anglicanum. My best service to your most Learned & obligeing Principal. Enquire what Mr Tanner is doing. The Lord bless you.
My Cosin Will Kirkby of Ashslack is lately dead. If you are ye waggoners servant, he'l be more careful of your Goods.
Direct your Goods unto Mr Thomas Brathwait at Kendal to be left with Mr John Gowling at ye Castle-Inn in Wood-street London to be sent by Kendal-Carrier.

note.value: 727. REV. GEORGE FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: I have receiv'd your kind Letters, & the Thirty Pounds by Tom. I should not have been thus long in Oxon~, but yt I am unwilling to be without Company in so long a journey. I hope my Boxes are now with you, I could wish, without any injury from ye waters; but for fear of ye worst, I desire they may be put in a dry place, such as is yt over ye Brew-house; or the Books taken out of ye Boxes. I desire yt such books as are wett may not be brought nigh ye fire, or open'd. The Box in which my Stud. Gown is I desire may be nail'd up again if you chare to open it, for its full of papers I would not willingly have seen. The Boxes are in number 7 & one of them James's. his Stud. Gown is in it. A Letter, Sr, from one of my Brothers giveing an account of what Quarter my Boxes have had, & meeting me at Park-House or Ingleton, would be very acceptable, for I am very uneasy till I hear what case my Books are in. So Sr desiring your blessing, rest
Your most oblig~d and obedt Son to Com~and

note.value: 731. BISHOP SMITH OF CARLISLE TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
This last week I recd yor kind L~re dated ye 8th Instant, and was very glad to hear of your & yor ffamily's good Health, wch I shall ever wish the continuance of. Yor son George is now wth me as my Chaplain, and I am very much pleas'd, as all here are, wth his conversation: After He had preach'd at Wigton, he went to his Parish where he stay'd over Whitsunday; but the next morning came hither wth Intenc~ons (I suppose) to continue wth us. About 3 days after, Mr Wiber (of whom I prsume you have heard) came also hither, in company of Mr Musgrave & another (younger) son of Sr Richard's from Hayton-Castle. I have entertain'd him likewise as my Chaplain, as I was before resolv'd to do, wch will make the
busienesse more easy to them & to mee too; being exceedingly wel satisfied wth them both.
My wife joins wth me in ye Return of our best Respects & Services to yor self & all yors at Ridal; and I am ever Worthy Sr,
ffor Sr Daniel Fleming Knt at Ridal This.

note.value: 744. DR. HENRY FLEMING TO SIR DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p:
Meetting last Thursday with the news of Mr Savage's death, I went that night to Penrith and yesterday morning to Rose in hopes
that the Bishop would ha' been as good as his word, and with desire of accepting of Caldbeck and quitting Grasmere: but I soon found that (contrary to truth and Honesty) Bro~. George was presented with the Prebendary, and Mr Wybergh with the liveing; so that I only told my mind a little to my Lord, (and came) home last night. Mr Wybergh must quitt Lamp-(lew so that) Brother Roger may probably gett it with timely (application.)

(I found my) wife a little troubled with a sore breast which we (thought was) occasion'd by cold, and wu'd soon mend; but last (night brought) me an account that it was burst. My Duty (and Ser)vice attends your self, my Brothers and Sisters, I am
For Sr Daniell Fleming att Rydal These.

note.value: 15. JOHN BANKES TO DANIEL FLEMING.

text.p: I would not willingly omit any Post but let you heare from Me wee have had not.

John And Mr Whartons to your father yor Ante Anderton did showe wh wth the order to Mr Wales who is Clarke to the Comissionrs in Preston but he said the Comissionrs would take noe notice off itt unlesse the Auditor had either inserted the words we desired or write a l~re under his hand: wch I could wish he had done ffor the Comissionrs are very Cautious of money the business is such a great arreare but I
hope by tomorrows Post wee shall receive the glad tydings of Allowance wch indeede I shall be glad to see: yet before the originall can be sued out I doe feare the wilbe very bussie wth vs: yet if it pleasse god that we have Allowance or so granted it may be there might be some vsed wth them to preuent them: Sr now our desire wilbe to resume the will or know where we may perceiue it: ffor the Comission is to be executed at Preston the 22th of this Instant where the will would be very necessary. Sir yor Mother is offe opinion that iff ther any motions of peace by Crosland and Collingwood if wee get our Clayme allowed it were ffit they weare imbrased to preuent ffuture inconveniences: Sir my younge Son is soe extreame sick this night that I doe beleiue if he continue the lord that gaue him will take him to his mercy: But I doe freely resigne him to him that gaue him.

Sir yor Ante Dudley hath been sroke but is pretty well recouered All frends in that contry are well. I have sent you herein enlossed
theise from yor Unkle Hudleston wch he desires that yu will be pleased to take notice off. Som moneyes wch yu haue disburst ffor him might be repayed againe by yor ffather out off the 5l~ yor Unkle left you at London. Yor ffather mother brothers and sister here are all well. My wife presents her respects to you. Thus wishinge Sir all health and happiness I rest as I am oblidged
Yor faithfull Servant in all obedience John Bankes Coniston this 8th Apprill 1653.
This ffor his euer honoured Maister Danyell fleming Esq at his Chamber at the Princes Armes in ffullers Rents neare Greys Inn London these left I pray
